nodes.label: Brownfield Classification Signals
nodes.rationale: ANY of: source files in a recognized language, framework config, package manifest with application dependencies, application source directories, or a parseable .gitmodules with at least one submodule path — repo metadata declares code even when the submodule dirs are not yet initialized.

nodes.label: Greenfield Classification Signals
nodes.rationale: ALL negative signals must hold. README, .gitignore, LICENSE, editor configs, empty dirs, CI/CD boilerplate without application code, the harness dir and aidlc/ never make a project brownfield, so framework scaffolding is not mistaken for the user's application.

nodes.label: In-Scope Phase Artifact Directories
nodes.rationale: A phase the scope excludes gets NO directory: an empty operation/ in a bugfix record would read as work planned and skipped when that phase was never in the plan. The phases present are exactly the phases the workflow will run; PHASE_SKIPPED audit events name the rest.

nodes.label: Space-Level Knowledge Directory
nodes.rationale: Free-form and empty at bootstrap, sibling of memory/, codekb/ and intents/, so team domain knowledge accumulates across every intent in the space rather than being trapped in one intent's record. Birth creates no per-agent subdirectories or seeded READMEs; the team creates them.

nodes.label: Brownfield versus Greenfield Grid Effect
nodes.rationale: The classification changes the WHOLE grid, not one stage: a brownfield feature leans on existing structure and can compress discovery, while a greenfield feature has nothing to reverse-engineer and everything to scope.

nodes.label: Entropy Scoring Before Selection
nodes.rationale: Estimate the five components (intent ambiguity, structural uncertainty, verification entropy, risk, unresolved assumptions) BEFORE looking at any stock scope, because the component bands rather than keyword vibes determine which stages carry positive expected value.

nodes.label: Folding Overlapping Stages
nodes.rationale: When two stages reduce the same entropy component, keep the spine (core, verification, and the single load-bearing discovery/design stage) and fold the framing stage whose output another EXECUTE stage already delivers - naming the un-SKIP trigger. Prefer a stock scope within a couple of stage flips, because a custom scope is maintenance surface the user owns forever.

nodes.label: Grid Discipline
nodes.rationale: Every required consume must have its producer on the EXECUTE set (validator-enforced, rejected in in-flight strict mode), and a starved input is never silently balanced by adding the producer - the addition is named in the rationale so the human sees the plan grow and why. Stages are data-coupled, so consumes/produces are checked before cutting anything mid-arc.

nodes.label: Incremental versus Net-New Task Shape
nodes.rationale: Work inside an existing system needs to understand what exists, define done, and change-plus-verify; it does not need market-research, user-stories, or application-design, because those discover and shape a product that already exists. Net-new surface needs the discovery arc in proportion to how much new structure it introduces.

nodes.label: Minimum Viable Workflow
nodes.rationale: Fit the ceremony to the task: the least sufficient EXECUTE set that still produces every artifact the outcome depends on. Both errors are real - skipping a load-bearing stage has a cost someone pays later, and including overlapping ceremony just in case collapses a composed grid back toward the stock feature scope and defeats composing. Neither default caution nor default economy is acceptable.

nodes.label: Nested-Project Fallback
nodes.rationale: When no top-level signal fires, descend one level into arbitrarily-named subdirectories and re-apply the same signal set, because a project whose source lives one container down (wordbook/, backend/) would otherwise be misclassified greenfield. Bounded to depth-1 and never run when the root already has a source signal, to keep the scan cheap and avoid pulling vendored or sibling projects into the classification.

nodes.label: Uninitialized Submodule Warning Relay
nodes.rationale: Relay verbatim and tell the user to run git submodule update --init --recursive, because reverse-engineering needs the code on disk. Advisory only: do not run the command and do not block auto-proceed.

nodes.label: Lazy Per-Stage Directory Creation
nodes.rationale: Per-stage dirs appear only when a stage first writes an artifact, so the record only ever shows stages that produced something. This is why reverse-engineering/ never appears up front — it writes its 9 deliverables to the space-level per-repo codekb store, leaving only its memory.md diary in the intent record.

nodes.label: Missing-Upstream Fallback for Incremental Scopes
nodes.rationale: security-patch and infra scopes skip environment-provisioning or build-and-test by design, because a brownfield production system already has environments and a deploy path. When those inputs are absent, inventory the real environments from workspace configuration and deploy through the pipeline that exists - never invent the content of a missing artifact.

nodes.label: feedback-loop Artifact
nodes.rationale: This is the final stage; the feedback loop document feeds insights back into the next Ideation cycle, which is why its approval gate carries a third option (Start New Ideation Cycle) that no other stage gate offers.

nodes.label: Golden Signals Question Set
nodes.rationale: Latency, traffic, errors, saturation drive dashboard and alarm design; SLO/SLI definitions, log retention rules, and distributed-tracing instrumentation are settled at the same gate so the emitted config is complete rather than incrementally patched.

nodes.label: Four Pillars of Observability
nodes.rationale: Metrics (RED for services, USE for resources), structured JSON logs with traceId and tiered retention, traces across services, and alerts on symptoms such as error rate rather than causes such as CPU - with a runbook link in every alert and P1/P2/P3 severity routing.

nodes.label: Pillar: Operational Excellence
nodes.rationale: Measured by MTTR. Infrastructure as code, observability, runbooks, deployment automation with automatic rollback, and game days that simulate failure. Anti-patterns named: console changes, error-only logging, no runbooks, Friday-afternoon deploys without monitoring.

nodes.label: Operational Outcome Trigger
nodes.rationale: Deployment, observability, incident-response and performance stages belong on the plan when the task's DONE lives in an environment rather than in the repo - a plan that builds but never ships closes no operational task.

nodes.label: DynamoDB Single-Table Design
nodes.rationale: Multiple entity types in one table using overloaded partition and sort keys with prefixes.

nodes.label: Global Secondary Index (GSI)
nodes.rationale: Different partition key, eventually consistent, consumes extra write capacity.

nodes.label: Local Secondary Index (LSI)
nodes.rationale: Same partition key, supports strong consistency, must be defined at table creation.

nodes.label: API Versioning Strategies
nodes.rationale: Version only on breaking changes; query-parameter versioning conflates filtering with contract selection.

nodes.label: Access-Pattern-First Design Process
nodes.rationale: Every access pattern is documented with the query it must serve before PK/SK patterns are designed.

nodes.label: Relational B-Tree Index Design
nodes.rationale: Index WHERE/JOIN/ORDER BY columns, most selective first, and avoid over-indexing because each index slows writes.

nodes.label: Data Migration Strategies
nodes.rationale: Always dry-run and compare row counts and checksums before committing.

nodes.label: Normalization Forms (1NF to BCNF)
nodes.rationale: Normalize to 3NF for transactional systems and denormalize selectively for read-heavy workloads.

nodes.label: Relational vs NoSQL Selection
nodes.rationale: Relational for complex reporting, ad-hoc queries and multi-table transactions; DynamoDB for well-defined access patterns and single-digit-ms latency at any scale.

nodes.label: Schema Versioning
nodes.rationale: A per-item schemaVersion lets application code read backward-compatibly across versions.

nodes.label: CodeKB Durable Per-Repo Knowledge Base
nodes.rationale: Space-level directory shared across intents, resolved by the codekb-path tool.

nodes.label: Rerun Overwrite Guard
nodes.rationale: The scope block is machine-read on the next run, so its accuracy decides whether a future intent is warned before overwriting this run's knowledge; component names are compared literally.

nodes.label: nfr-validation-matrix Artifact
nodes.rationale: Target versus actual per NFR, so the Operation phase closes the loop on the quantified targets nfr-requirements declared rather than asserting performance narratively.

nodes.label: NFR-to-Architecture Mapping
nodes.rationale: Each quantified NFR is translated into concrete structure - sub-100ms latency into caching and async non-blocking I/O, 99.9% availability into multi-AZ plus health checks plus circuit breakers, RTO under an hour into multi-region active-passive with tested runbooks, zero-downtime deploys into blue-green or canary with backward-compatible migrations.

nodes.label: CDK Assertion and Snapshot Testing
nodes.rationale: Fine-grained assertions cover security properties, critical configuration and resource counts; snapshots catch regressions and make infrastructure diffs reviewable in pull requests. CDK internals and CloudFormation implementation details are explicitly not tested.

nodes.label: CDK Construct Levels (L1/L2/L3)
nodes.rationale: L2 is preferred because it encodes AWS best practices as defaults and adds grant helpers; L1 only when L2 hides a needed property; L3 only when the pattern fits exactly - significant customization means dropping back to L2.

nodes.label: Environment-Aware Stacks
nodes.rationale: One codebase for all environments with differences parameterized through context-driven config; account IDs and regions are never hardcoded, and production stacks must declare an explicit account and region rather than relying on ambient defaults.

nodes.label: Props Interface Pattern
nodes.rationale: Dependencies arrive via readonly props rather than being created inside the construct, and props are typed as interfaces (IVpc, ITable) rather than concrete types because that is what enables cross-stack references. Outputs are exposed as public readonly for consuming constructs.

nodes.label: CDK Security Defaults
nodes.rationale: Encryption on S3/DynamoDB/SQS/EBS, BLOCK_ALL public access, authorization on every API route, access and execution logging with explicit retention, and least privilege expressed through grant helpers rather than hand-written wildcard IAM policies.

nodes.label: Stack Organization by Lifecycle
nodes.rationale: Resources that change together share a stack; stateful resources (databases, buckets) are separated from stateless compute because stateful stacks change rarely while stateless stacks deploy frequently. Cross-stack references are used sparingly since they create deployment coupling.

nodes.label: Container Orchestration Checklist
nodes.rationale: Pinned minimal base image, multi-stage build, health endpoint, SIGTERM draining, CPU/memory limits against noisy neighbours, secrets from a manager rather than the image or env vars, stdout/stderr logging, non-root user, read-only filesystem where possible.

nodes.label: Deployment Strategy Selection
nodes.rationale: Blue-green buys instant rollback for double infrastructure cost and schema-sync complexity; canary limits blast radius but needs traffic splitting and automated metric comparison; rolling needs no extra infrastructure but runs mixed versions and rolls back slower; recreate is simplest but takes downtime.

nodes.label: IaC Tool Selection
nodes.rationale: CDK for AWS-native TypeScript/Python teams accepting lock-in, Terraform for multi-cloud accepting state-management complexity, CloudFormation when CDK is overkill, Pulumi for polyglot teams, Docker Compose for local development only - never production orchestration.

nodes.label: Standard CI/CD Pipeline Stages
nodes.rationale: Fourteen ordered stages each with a time budget so the pipeline fails fast: lint under 30s, build under 2 min, unit tests under 3 min, SAST blocking on high/critical, E2E on critical paths only with flaky tests quarantined rather than skipped, and artifacts tagged with the commit SHA.

nodes.label: Pillar: Security
nodes.rationale: IAM roles over long-lived keys with MFA and least privilege, CloudTrail/GuardDuty/Security Hub/Config for detection, KMS at rest and TLS 1.2+ in transit, private subnets and VPC endpoints, pre-provisioned forensics. Anti-patterns: wildcard policies, secrets in env vars or code, public buckets or 0.0.0.0/0 groups, unencrypted stores.

nodes.label: Audit Trail Requirements
nodes.rationale: The one requirement common to every framework: CloudTrail in all regions and accounts to a centralized immutable Object Lock bucket, application-level who-did-what-when logs with authentication context, integrity validation, framework-specific retention (PCI 1 year, HIPAA 6 years), and meta-auditing of access to the logs themselves.

nodes.label: Breadcrumbs

nodes.label: Approval gates (HARD STOP, no emergent behavior)
nodes.norm_label: approval gates (hard stop, no emergent behavior)

nodes.label: Reviewer dispatch record (.aidlc-reviewer-dispatch.json)
nodes.rationale: The record is where the spot-check carve-out is granted and is what lets a PreToolUse hook enforce the reviewer read-scope bound deterministically instead of trusting prose; it is deleted after the review because a leftover record would keep refusing sibling access for later unrelated work.

nodes.label: TEC_Project governance overlay
nodes.rationale: AI-DLC approval and TEC governance are deliberately separate: AI-DLC may declare a stage complete, but only the human student/supervisor may accept the TEC gate after reading the governance report, and a FAIL or NOT REVIEWABLE verdict forbids approving, advancing, or mutating the artifact.

nodes.label: Architecture Reviewer Agent
nodes.rationale: Reviews with fresh eyes and no access to the builder's plan.md or memory.md, intentionally, so the judgment is independent; READY means a developer could implement without architectural guidance beyond the document, not that the design is perfect.

nodes.label: Product Lead Agent (review-only)
nodes.rationale: Reviews but never produces, so the customer's and business's voice at the quality gate is structurally independent of the builder; vagueness is challenged ruthlessly because an untestable requirement is a wish.

nodes.label: Adversarial review posture (refute, do not confirm)
nodes.norm_label: adversarial review posture (refute, do not confirm)
nodes.rationale: READY is the verdict reached only after hunting for defects fails, not the starting point; and every finding must be grounded in checkable evidence because a finding backed only by architectural taste is a suggestion, not grounds for NOT-READY.

nodes.label: Reviewer read-scope bound (no sibling-unit sweeps)
nodes.rationale: Cross-unit soundness is verified against the passed shared inception contracts rather than by browsing sibling units, so the reviewer's context stays bounded; the only carve-out is opening the single file that owns an explicitly named integration point, resolved via the contracts rather than by directory browsing.

nodes.label: Advisory dispatch (single pass, findings go to the human gate)
nodes.norm_label: advisory dispatch (single pass, findings go to the human gate)
nodes.rationale: An advisory pass is decision support rather than a repair loop, so the refute-until-READY posture is dropped while evidence-grounding is kept; a Request Changes at the human gate is how an advisory finding becomes a revision, and the verdict line informs rather than gates.

nodes.label: Reviewer invocation (12a): adversarial and advisory review classes
nodes.norm_label: reviewer invocation (12a): adversarial and advisory review classes
nodes.rationale: Adversarial is the default where findings are machine-checkable and fix loops converge (Construction); advisory is the default for human-gated prose stages where readiness is a judgment call that belongs to the human at the gate. The reviewer never blocks the workflow and never sees the builder's plan or diary, so its judgment is independent while the human keeps final say. On a NOT-READY the LEAD alone is re-invoked, not the whole ensemble, because review findings are artifact defects and the lead owns the artifacts.

nodes.label: Voice contract (narrate the work, not the plumbing)

nodes.label: Serverless
nodes.rationale: Fits event-driven work, bursty or long-idle traffic, and rapid prototyping. Functions stay stateless and idempotent because events may be delivered more than once, and concurrency limits protect downstream systems. Cold-start latency, vendor lock-in to the provider runtime, and the 15-minute execution ceiling are the accepted costs.

nodes.label: Verdict Rules
nodes.rationale: READY requires zero Critical and at most two Major with any number of Minor; a mechanical threshold rather than reviewer mood, so repeat iterations converge instead of drifting.

nodes.label: Compute Rightsizing
nodes.rationale: Compute Optimizer after 14 days of data, resized in non-production first. Most teams over-provision by 30-50% at initial deployment, Graviton gives 20-40% better price-performance, and non-production instances are scheduled off outside business hours.

nodes.label: Cost Reviews and Anomaly Detection
nodes.rationale: Monthly reviews by service, tag, daily trend and usage type, plus Cost Anomaly Detection and budget alerts at 50/80/100% with separate budgets per environment, so a spike is caught in days rather than at the invoice.

nodes.label: DynamoDB Capacity Mode Selection
nodes.rationale: On-Demand for spiky or new tables, provisioned with auto-scaling plus reserved capacity for steady production. TTL deletions carry no write cost, and evenly distributed partition keys matter for cost because hot partitions waste provisioned capacity.

nodes.label: Lambda Cost Optimization
nodes.rationale: Because cost is memory x duration x invocations and more memory also means more CPU, raising memory can lower total cost - Power Tuning finds the point. arm64 saves about 20%, SQS batching and EventBridge content filtering cut invocation counts, and provisioned concurrency is avoided unless latency demands it.

nodes.label: AWS Pricing Model Selection
nodes.rationale: Compute Savings Plans cover the baseline because they span EC2, Lambda and Fargate; On-Demand absorbs the peaks; Reserved Instances only for very predictable instance types. Spot buys up to 90% off for interruption-tolerant work and is never used for databases or single-instance workloads.

nodes.label: Pillar: Cost Optimization
nodes.rationale: Visibility through Cost Explorer, budgets and allocation tags; rightsizing from Compute Optimizer; Savings Plans for steady state and Spot for fault-tolerant work; storage lifecycle transitions; and waste elimination (idle instances, unattached volumes, unused Elastic IPs).

nodes.label: Pillar: Performance Efficiency
nodes.rationale: Right-size by measurement rather than guesswork, cache at the appropriate layer, match the database engine to the access pattern, offload long tasks asynchronously, and load test at 2-3x expected peak. Without a performance baseline, degradation cannot be detected at all.

nodes.label: Well-Architected Review Process
nodes.rationale: Mandatory before production launch and quarterly for critical workloads: scope one workload, walk each pillar's questions with the team, identify high-risk issues, prioritize by risk and effort, assign owners and deadlines, then re-review to verify closure.

nodes.label: Pillar: Sustainability
nodes.rationale: Graviton for performance per watt, scale-to-demand and scheduled non-production shutdowns, managed and serverless services that pool utilization across customers, and deleting unnecessary data - the same levers as cost optimization measured as resources per unit of work.

nodes.label: AWS Cost Optimization Patterns
nodes.rationale: Cost optimization is an ongoing discipline, not a one-time exercise.

nodes.label: AWS Well-Architected Framework
nodes.rationale: Six pillars, each with a headline metric, used at architecture reviews, before production launches, and periodically for existing workloads.

nodes.label: Supervisor (freeze-gate countersign authority)
nodes.rationale: Does not gate day-to-day scope, which the student takes alone and the supervisor countersigns after the fact; does gate every freeze gate, because a freeze-gate value must be resolved, recorded and approved before the affected work begins and no agent or implementer may supply one.

nodes.label: AI-DLC Method Import Stub
nodes.rationale: A reference, never a copy: the layered method (org/team/project plus the four phase files) is authored once under the workspace memory tree, and this stub pulls it into ambient context so casual chat outside a stage still sees standing practices. Claude imports name one explicit file each (no globs), resolve relative to this file, and chain up to four hops, so a new method file needs a matching import line. Ships pointed at the always-present default space; /aidlc space <name> re-points these lines in place, a byte-identical no-op at default. AI-DLC's own stage resolver reads the same tree directly and never needs the stub.

nodes.label: AskUserQuestion Harness Binding
nodes.rationale: The one place that binds the harness-neutral structured-question contract to a concrete mechanism: the fenced question spec maps 1:1 onto AskUserQuestion fields (prompt/header/multiSelect/options label+description). Keeping the binding in a single annex is what lets the protocol and stage files stay harness-neutral. Harness specifics live here too: the approval gate's next-stage placeholder is rendered verbatim from the directive's next_stage field (Complete workflow when null) and never guessed, and the user's selection is recorded as the exact option label.

nodes.label: Question Batching Limits
nodes.rationale: Max four questions per call, max four options per question, and at least two options - a one-option call is rejected by the tool before the user can answer. Five or more options are split across calls (A-D, then E+) while the questions file retains the full option set as the authoritative record.

nodes.label: Consolidated-Summary Checkpoint Rendering
nodes.rationale: Two semantic options with no A/B file-letter prefixes, presented as its own turn that ENDS: a lettered, numbered, bare-letter or self-selected answer is invalid, so the letter and description are stripped before writing. On Request changes the conductor asks what should change and ends the turn again, refusing to touch any answer until that feedback arrives, then resets the tag and re-presents. No artifact is generated until the file holds the explicit answer and the receipt command succeeds.

nodes.label: Built-in Other Escape
nodes.rationale: Because AskUserQuestion always offers Other, an explicit Other option must NOT be added to interactive batches - while questions files still end every question with 'X. Other (please specify)' per protocol, since the file format is harness-neutral and cannot rely on a harness affordance.

nodes.label: ask Directive
nodes.rationale: The engine never calls AskUserQuestion itself - it defers the human turn to the conductor, who renders directive.question and feeds the verbatim answer back on the next report via --user-input. Any resume-menu answer reports result resumed and then acts on the returned per-choice print.

nodes.label: Autonomy Is Never Inferred
nodes.rationale: 'Go with recommended' is a one-time instruction for that stage only; the next stage starts fresh, autonomy is never carried forward, and questions are never self-answered without explicit permission for the specific stage.

nodes.label: Learnings Ritual
nodes.rationale: surface, then a structured question plus free-text channel, then an admission conflict-check against org.md, then persist. The 'Anything to add?' question must carry at least two explicit options and is asked even when surface returns zero candidates, because inferring 'Nothing to add' would let the loop silently skip the only sanctioned path for turning a human correction into a persistent practice in team.md or project.md.

nodes.label: load-steering Directive
nodes.rationale: Transport, not stage work: rules_content is applied in array order and retained as the active bundle, then continue is called with the continue_token, repeating until run-stage. It is never reported, and loading rules is deliberately unspoken because it is not an event in the user's project.

nodes.label: Parking a Workflow
nodes.rationale: An enterprise-scope run need not finish in one session: park stops cleanly at the current inter-stage boundary, advancing nothing and marking nothing complete, and exists so a low-context conductor never fabricates approvals to reach done. Resume is /aidlc --resume, which clears the park marker.

nodes.label: PRE-GENERATION SUMMARY STOP
nodes.rationale: A mandatory human checkpoint after any file-backed Q&A and before any artifact exists: append the Consolidated Summary Confirmation section, record the prompt with a checkpoint-specific decision receipt, render the unlettered Looks correct / Request changes choice, and treat Q&A as incomplete until the file holds the human's exact answer and the receipt command succeeds. It is not bypassed even on the isolated single-stage path, and it never merges with the reviewer, learnings or approval steps.

nodes.label: Stage Ritual Atomicity
nodes.rationale: Once a stage starts every step fires - questions, artifact, reviewer, learnings, gate - and none is skippable. 'Skip to stage X' skips intermediate stages, never the target's own ritual, and the current stage including learnings must complete before jumping.

nodes.label: Typed Directive
nodes.rationale: Exactly one JSON directive per next call, whose kind names the single move to make. Eight kinds are emitted today (load-steering, run-stage, invoke-swarm, ask, print, error, done, parked); dispatch-subagent and present-gate remain documented placeholders so the loop is complete-shaped, and implementing them speculatively is forbidden.

nodes.rationale: Written at the workspace root, deliberately outside the intent record dir, because it is the team's operating artefact rather than part of the audited workflow record.

nodes.label: Audit Shard Event Trail
nodes.rationale: Every .md shard under <record>/audit/ is the full event trail; events are ordered by their Timestamp fields to build the narrative, and are used for prose only — never for counts the summary tool already reports.

nodes.label: runtime-graph.json Event-Sourced View
nodes.rationale: The materialised, event-sourced view the summary command reads; it exists only after a workflow's first stage transition compiles it, which is why every read-only skill has an explicit non-zero-exit fallback message.

nodes.label: AI-DLC Outcomes Pack Skill
nodes.rationale: Produces a single handover document at workflow close so the team can own, operate and keep building the delivered system without re-running the workflow to recover context.

nodes.label: AI-DLC Session Replay Skill
nodes.rationale: Renders to the terminal only and writes no file, so a replay can be run freely mid-workflow; users who want a saved artefact are pointed at /aidlc-outcomes-pack instead of duplicating a writer here.

nodes.label: AI-DLC Session Cost Skill
nodes.rationale: Gives a transparent, deterministic view of workflow consumption; does no counting of its own, does not walk the artefact tree, and prints fields verbatim without recomputing or rounding, so the report cannot drift from the tool.

nodes.label: Commit vs Archive Policy
nodes.rationale: Decisions, architecture summary and NFR table are committed into docs/; audit shards go to a compliance archive and are explicitly NOT committed to the application repo; question files and aidlc-state.md are discarded because they are workflow scaffolding, not deliverables.

nodes.label: Tool-Sourced Counting Rule
nodes.rationale: Stage tallies, per-phase rollup, memory-entry counts and learnings must trace to the tool's output rather than to eyeballing the artefact tree; prose stays the model's job, counts stay the tool's, so no number in a report is invented.

nodes.label: Session Replay Narrative
nodes.rationale: Turns the audit trail into a readable story of what was decided, in what order and why — explicitly not a raw log dump — for async review and stakeholders who were not in the room.

nodes.label: Read-Only Skill Classification
nodes.rationale: classification: read-only means the skill never advances the workflow stage pointer and never emits an audit event, which is what makes it safe to run at any point in a workflow, including mid-stage.

nodes.label: Deliberate Token-Estimate Omission
nodes.rationale: The skill deliberately prints no token estimate: the retired file-size-to-token heuristic was guesswork dressed as data. Real token accounting must come from the Claude Code session, not a file-size approximation.

nodes.label: Compliance-as-Code Patterns
nodes.rationale: Automate verification instead of relying on manual audits: Config rules and conformance packs per framework, Security Hub aggregation and scoring, cdk-nag enforcing rules at synthesis time (AwsSolutions, NIST80053R5, HIPAASecurity, PCIDSS321 check packs), and Lambda-backed custom rules for organization-specific requirements.

nodes.label: Data Residency and Sovereignty
nodes.rationale: Residency is where data is stored; sovereignty is whose law then applies to it. Enforced with region-restricting SCPs, bucket and table placement, and cross-region replication that respects residency - with documented cross-region data flows for audits.

nodes.label: GDPR
nodes.rationale: Applies by data subject residency, not company location. Six principles plus five data subject rights translate into engineering work: DSAR automation, soft-delete with configurable retention, DynamoDB TTL or S3 lifecycle for automatic expiry, and tagged PII stores for governance.

nodes.label: HIPAA
nodes.rationale: A BAA is required before storing PHI and only HIPAA-eligible services may be used, verified per service. Encryption at rest and in transit satisfies Safe Harbor, audit logs retain 6 years, breach notification runs within 60 days, and PHI is isolated in dedicated accounts or VPCs with PrivateLink so it never traverses the public internet.

nodes.label: PCI-DSS
nodes.rationale: Twelve requirements mapped to AWS controls, with scope reduction as the highest-leverage move: tokenizing through a compliant processor so raw card numbers never enter the system makes most requirements inapplicable rather than merely satisfied. Log retention at least one year.

nodes.label: Privacy Impact Assessment
nodes.rationale: Five steps run when processing is introduced or materially changed: describe the processing, test proportionality (could the same outcome be reached with less data), identify risks including function creep, define mitigations, then document and review annually.

nodes.label: SOC 2
nodes.rationale: Type I attests design at a point in time and is faster; Type II attests operating effectiveness over 6-12 months and is more valued. Security is the only mandatory Trust Service Criterion; evidence collection is automated with Config conformance packs and Security Hub rather than gathered by hand.

nodes.rationale: With ANTHROPIC_API_KEY set the skill uses the Anthropic Python SDK directly and spawns no subprocess; without it, it falls back to the claude CLI and reuses the user's existing desktop authentication.

nodes.label: 500KB File Size Limit
nodes.rationale: Files over 500KB are rejected before any API call is made, so an oversized input cannot become an unbounded request.

nodes.label: claude CLI Subprocess Fallback
nodes.rationale: subprocess.run() invokes the claude CLI only when ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is unset, using a fixed argument list with user file content passed on stdin rather than as a shell argument, so no shell interpolation can occur.

nodes.label: Validate-and-Cherry-Pick Compression Pipeline
nodes.rationale: detect type -> compress -> validate (headings, code blocks, URLs, file paths, bullets) -> cherry-pick targeted fixes only, never a recompression -> retry up to 2 times -> if still failing, report and leave the original untouched. Patching only broken parts avoids a second full-file token spend and stops a retry from introducing new drift.

nodes.label: Compressible File-Type Boundaries
nodes.rationale: Only .md/.txt/.rst/.typ/.typst/.tex and extensionless prose are compressed; code and config (.py/.js/.ts/.json/.yaml/.toml/.env/.lock/.css/.html/.xml/.sql/.sh) are never modified; mixed files have prose compressed only; anything ambiguous is left unchanged; *.original.md is always skipped.

nodes.label: Code Regions Are Read-Only
nodes.rationale: Fenced and inline code must be copied exactly — no removing comments or spacing, no reordering, no shortening commands. URLs, file paths, commands, technical terms, proper nouns, dates, versions and environment variables are likewise preserved verbatim; headings keep exact text while only the body beneath is compressed.

nodes.label: Caveman Compress Overview
nodes.rationale: Shrink the memory file, save tokens every session. Only two steps spend tokens (initial compression, plus a targeted cherry-picked fix when validation fails); everything else — type detection, validation, writing — is local Python.

nodes.label: Caveman Compress Skill
nodes.rationale: Compresses natural-language memory files into caveman-speak to cut input tokens; the compressed version overwrites the original so the file Claude actually reads is the small one.

nodes.label: 46% Average Context-Token Savings
nodes.rationale: CLAUDE.md loads on every session start, so a 1000-token memory file is recurring overhead — 100 sessions is 100,000 tokens for context already written. Benchmarked 36.9%-59.6% reduction across five real files, 46% average, with headings, code blocks, URLs and file paths preserved exactly.

nodes.label: Snyk High-Risk Rating False Positive
nodes.rationale: The High Risk rating comes from static-analysis heuristics firing on subprocess plus file read/write patterns. The skill does not execute file content as code, makes no network requests except to Anthropic's API, touches no path outside the user-provided file and its backup dir, and never uses shell=True or string interpolation.

nodes.label: Out-of-Tree Original Backup
nodes.rationale: The human-readable FILE.original.md backup lives in $XDG_DATA_HOME/caveman-compress/backups/<parent-dir-name>/ (or %LOCALAPPDATA%\caveman-compress\backups\<parent-dir-name>\ on Windows) rather than beside the source, so skill auto-loaders do not re-ingest the uncompressed copy as a live file — which would cancel the token saving.

nodes.rationale: How support agents join is governed by directive.mode, never by the mere presence of support_agents, because the topology is who-talks-to-whom rather than who-participates. The conductor is the bus on every topology and agents never invoke each other, which keeps every inter-agent message an auditable dispatch. nodes.norm_label: engine-resolved artifact paths (no stage file hardcodes a root)

nodes.label: Swarm-trigger field coupling (for_each + mode)
nodes.rationale: The autonomous Construction swarm fires on a field match rather than an explicit flag, so re-moding the per-unit build stage silently takes it off the swarm path; the compiler emits an advisory on stderr precisely because the coupling is implicit.

nodes.label: Terminal review receipt and review freeze
nodes.norm_label: terminal review receipt and review freeze
nodes.rationale: Once a terminal receipt is recorded, writing to a produces[] artifact invalidates it and the engine refuses the gate, so a reviewed artifact cannot be quietly edited after review. Riding suggestions are quoted verbatim for the human instead of applied, since a suggestion was explicitly not grounds for NOT-READY and therefore is not grounds for editing past the receipt either. The precondition is hard on the review having happened and soft on its verdict.

nodes.label: Consistent Error Response Envelope

nodes.label: HATEOAS Links

nodes.label: URL Naming Conventions
nodes.rationale: Plural nouns, shallow nesting, kebab-case, no verbs - HTTP methods convey the action.

nodes.label: PHASE_VERIFIED Audit Event
nodes.rationale: Recorded by the engine into the active record's audit/<host>-<clone-id>.md shard and explicitly never appended by hand, keeping the audit trail tool-owned so a prose-written receipt cannot claim a verification that never ran.

nodes.label: Phase Check Report
nodes.rationale: Written per boundary as verification/phase-check-<phase>.md carrying coverage percentages, warnings, consistency checks and a human approval checkbox, so the verdict is a reviewable artifact and the human, not the tool, accepts the boundary.

nodes.label: Phase Boundary Verification
nodes.rationale: Verification fires at each phase boundary (Ideation to Inception, Inception to Construction, Construction to Operation), on demand, and as a lightweight stage-completion self-check, because gaps between phases are invisible to per-stage checking: each boundary check asks whether the downstream artifacts actually consume the upstream ones.

nodes.label: Traceability Matrix
nodes.rationale: Maps Intent to Requirement to Story to Architecture Component to Code Module to Test Suite, with three status indicators (fully traced, partially traced, orphan) so a broken chain is named at a specific link rather than reported as a global percentage.

nodes.label: Never Echo the question Spec
nodes.rationale: A question fence is input to the tool, never output to render, and echoing it is a protocol violation rather than a style choice: it produces a wall of text the user cannot click, loses the tool's built-in Other escape, and is inconsistent with every correct rendering in the same session. Applies to every structured-question site - approval gates, interaction-mode choice, the ladder prompt, halt-and-ask, summary confirmation, the learnings gate. Fences in framework documentation are authoring specs, not chat output, so they legitimately remain.

nodes.label: Audit Event Naming Discipline
nodes.rationale: Event types come only from the shared audit-format reference and are never invented. State transitions are tool-owned: the engine's report step and the stage tools own every emission, and no audit event is ever written from prose - so each lifecycle outcome is reported exactly once and a speculative direct lifecycle call hits the state guard.

nodes.label: The Forwarding Loop
nodes.rationale: The orchestrator's whole control structure: next, act, report, repeat until done. The split exists so all between-stage routing (scope resolution, flag precedence, jump direction, resume/init guards, sequencing, gate status, completion) is owned deterministically by the tool and never re-derived in prose, leaving the conductor only the quality of execution inside the named move. next is read-only and mutates nothing; report commits the transition so the next next reads fresh state. A malformed directive is reported plainly and stops the loop rather than being improvised around.

nodes.label: narration Field
nodes.rationale: Worded by the tool that knows the facts: when present it is what the user hears about the step, reproduced with only tense/name corrections and never accompanied by a further account of the mechanism; when absent the step is carried out silently. Speech is carried by exactly two things - a narration value between steps and a SAY line's quoted text inside a step - with one exception, the very first turn, where no next has returned yet and a single sentence about the user's own request is allowed.

nodes.label: Mandatory Protocol Loading
nodes.rationale: Three protocols load at fixed moments rather than on judgement: the stage protocol on every stage, the recovery protocol on session resume or a mid-stage change event, and the governance protocol at phase boundaries to run the phase-boundary traceability verification.

nodes.label: Quiet-In-Between Voice Rule
nodes.rationale: An expert working alongside someone does not narrate keystrokes, so the resting state between tool calls is no prose at all. The rule bites on paraphrase as well as jargon: a friendlier phrasing of internal routing is still that sentence. The working test - when a sentence's only content is which step comes next, make the tool call instead - and the Construction carve-out (iteration passes, continuation tokens, produces lists all stay internal) both follow from it.

nodes.label: bugfix Scope
nodes.rationale: Minimal depth, skeleton off, review cap advisory, 7 of 32 stages. Skips ideation entirely because there is no new product to discover; keeps reverse-engineering (understand what exists), requirements-analysis (state what fixed means), then code-generation and build-and-test. Keywords fix/bug/broken are word-boundary matched so debug and fixture do not trigger it.

nodes.label: enterprise Scope
nodes.rationale: Comprehensive depth, 32 of 32 EXECUTE, and the reference column of the EXECUTE/SKIP grid that every other scope is a subset of. Runs every stage because for regulated work the cost of an undocumented decision exceeds the cost of running the stage. Deliberately has no keyword triggers, so it is chosen explicitly and never inferred.

nodes.label: feature Scope
nodes.rationale: Standard depth over the same 32-stage grid as enterprise: the difference is depth expressed in stage bodies and rule layers, not stage membership. It is the detector's catch-all fallback when freeform text carries no scope keyword or reads like a project description (the >5-word heuristic), so it carries no keywords of its own.

nodes.label: infra Scope
nodes.rationale: The one scope that leans on the back half of the graph (13 of 32): skips ideation and the application-code stages, runs practices-discovery, the NFR pass, infrastructure-design, ci-pipeline and the full deployment/observability set. Uniquely SKIPs reverse-engineering because infra changes start from deployment topology rather than application source, and it is the only non-enterprise/feature scope that runs the operation phase.

nodes.label: mvp Scope
nodes.rationale: Standard depth, 22 of 32: trims the discovery overhead that only pays off at scale (market-research, team-formation, approval-handoff) and skips the operation phase wholesale, keeping full inception and construction because an MVP is still real software. Promotes to feature or enterprise when it graduates.

nodes.label: poc Scope
nodes.rationale: Minimal depth, advisory review cap, 8 of 32. A spike answers one question - can this work? - so it keeps only intent-capture, reverse-engineering, requirements-analysis, code-generation and build-and-test. Discarding the design and operation ceremony is the point, because the artifact is throwaway; a yes answer means re-scoping to feature or mvp for the real build.

nodes.label: refactor Scope
nodes.rationale: Minimal depth, skeleton off, 8 of 32. Like bugfix it skips ideation and operation, but adds functional-design back because a refactor reshapes structure and the design of the behaviour being preserved matters; build-and-test verifies the existing suite stays green.

nodes.label: security-patch Scope
nodes.rationale: Minimal depth, 10 of 32, skeleton off. Skips the whole design ceremony because the change is targeted, but unlike bugfix keeps deployment-pipeline and deployment-execution EXECUTE, since a patch that never deploys does not close the vulnerability. requirements-analysis runs to give an auditable statement of the vulnerability and its remediation criteria, and nfr-requirements runs to record the security constraint.

nodes.label: workshop Scope
nodes.rationale: Standard depth with a testStrategy: Minimal override (25 of 32): participants must see the whole inception-construction-operation arc, so the substantive stages stay visible, while the early ideation ceremony is skipped because a facilitator front-loads scoping by hand. The test override means tests are demonstrated, not held to the production floor.

nodes.label: Scope-to-Stage Mapping
nodes.rationale: Source of truth is one file per scope under .claude/scopes/ (identity, keywords, description, skeleton default) plus each stage's scopes: frontmatter for membership, transposed into the compiled grid by aidlc-graph.ts compile. The in-skill table is regenerated human-readable data, explicitly not dispatch logic and never hand-edited; the one sanctioned write path is the composer appending an approved composed scope.

nodes.label: Scope membership grid (EXECUTE/SKIP transpose)
nodes.rationale: Each stage names the scopes it belongs to and the compile step transposes those declarations into the EXECUTE/SKIP grid, so scope membership is authored once per stage instead of maintained as a separate matrix that could disagree.

nodes.label: Compiled stage graph (stage-graph.json)
nodes.rationale: AI-DLC is open-world (plugins add stages, scopes, agents), so a compiled artefact plus /aidlc --doctor is the authoritative live view of what is enabled rather than any prose count.

nodes.label: Composer Agent (adaptive workflow composer)
nodes.rationale: It is a scoring function, not a research agent: the output is a per-stage EXECUTE/SKIP grid grounded by five coarse scores, so it stops gathering evidence as soon as it can score confidently (target under four tool calls with CodeKB present) rather than mapping the codebase itself.

nodes.label: Single structural evidence path (CodeKB-first, never blended)
nodes.norm_label: single structural evidence path (codekb-first, never blended)
nodes.rationale: CSU and the structural signals feeding VE draw from exactly one source, decided before scoring, because blending a pre-computed index with an ad-hoc scan produces incomparable evidence. When CodeKB is ready it REPLACES direct code scanning rather than supplementing it; the fallback scan is used only when CodeKB is absent, unindexed, or stale, and CodeKB is not re-attempted once fallback begins.

nodes.label: Compile + drift invariant (aidlc-graph compile --check)
nodes.rationale: CI re-runs the compile in memory and diffs against the checked-in JSON, so drift between the YAML sources and the compiled graph is impossible while the check passes.

nodes.label: consumes_absent (absence-by-design arrives as data)
nodes.rationale: Required inputs whose files are missing move to consumes_absent annotated expected true/false depending on whether the scope deliberately skipped the producer, and an absent optional consume is simply dropped, so the conductor is never pointed at an unreadable path and absence-by-design never surfaces as a failed read.

nodes.label: Caveman Review Boundaries
nodes.rationale: Reviews only: it does not write the fix, does not approve or request changes, and does not run linters, so the skill cannot silently take an authoring or gatekeeping action.

nodes.label: One-Line Review Comment Format
nodes.rationale: Each finding compresses to location, problem, fix so the actionable signal survives and the reviewer is not made to re-read what the diff already shows.

nodes.label: Review Severity Prefix Taxonomy
nodes.rationale: bug/risk/nit/q prefixes replace hedging prose: 'nit' carries the 'just a suggestion' meaning in four characters and 'q' carries genuine uncertainty, so terseness never turns into false confidence.

nodes.label: Finding Content Requirements
nodes.rationale: Each finding must carry a stable ID, cited evidence path, observed fact versus requirement, severity, affected gate and stage, consequence, smallest acceptable remediation, and the verification that closes it; unsupported criticism, invented scientific values, and generic best-practice or style-only findings are rejected.

nodes.label: Auto-Clarity Escape Hatch
nodes.rationale: Terse mode is dropped for security findings, architectural disagreements, and onboarding contexts because CVE-class bugs and design arguments need the rationale, not a one-liner; compression resumes afterwards.

nodes.label: Component Accessibility Requirements
nodes.rationale: ARIA role, keyboard interaction, labelling, contrast ratio, screen reader announcement, focus management.

nodes.label: Component State Table
nodes.rationale: Default, hover, focus, disabled, loading, error, and empty each with description and trigger.

nodes.label: Report Supersession Rule
nodes.rationale: Every review gets a new report ID; a prior gate report is never overwritten but superseded with an explicit link, and after remediation the board reruns against the new version while the previous report is preserved.

nodes.label: Authority And Evidence Table
nodes.rationale: Missing evidence is listed explicitly and a version or hash is never inferred.

nodes.label: Traceability And Downstream Impact
nodes.rationale: Every affected requirement, decision, test, dataset, feature, mask, experiment and artifact ID is listed, naming what is invalidated or must be regenerated, so a passed gate cannot silently leave stale downstream artifacts.

nodes.label: Authority Precedence Order
nodes.rationale: Vision normative core outranks Technical Environment, which outranks freeze decisions and change records, then AI-DLC stage artifacts, then code/tests/manifests/measured outputs, with reviewer inference last. A Vision/Technical Environment conflict is a blocking finding and is never resolved by inference.

nodes.label: Semantic Manifest Stamping
nodes.rationale: Only semantic files that actually produced output are stamped: a detected doc whose chunk failed must stay unstamped so the next --update re-queues it, otherwise it is marked done and its content is lost forever.

nodes.label: Graph Shrink Guard
nodes.rationale: to_json refuses to write when the new graph has fewer nodes than the existing graph.json, so a failed or empty extraction cannot clobber a good graph, report, or analysis sidecar; the guard message is surfaced rather than forced past.

nodes.label: research-pipeline-governed Scope
nodes.rationale: A composed scope (17 execute, 15 folded or skipped) for reproducible research pipeline work on a frozen data contract. Comprehensive depth is kept despite the lean grid because a governance board reads the surviving artifacts and a gate verdict turns on evidence quality, not stage count. Ships keywords: [] so it is resolvable only by explicit --scope and never participates in inference. Notable choices: reverse-engineering skips because CodeKB is the structural evidence source; the NFR pair stays unfolded because reproducibility, determinism and evaluation correctness interact and are reviewed as evidence; performance-validation is the deliverable rather than an afterthought; user-stories and mockups skip for lack of personas and UI; skeleton off because the frozen data contract leaves nothing to bootstrap.

nodes.label: TEC Governance Overlay
nodes.rationale: Deliberately NOT encoded in the scope file: the overlay is a project-level rule that gates human approval of each stage independently of AI-DLC's own completion signal. Comprehensive depth exists in the scope precisely so each stage's artifacts are reviewable at that external board.

nodes.label: Adaptive Workflow Composer
nodes.rationale: Dispatched as an agent that runs a read-only detect scan and estimates five entropy components, then proposes an EXECUTE/SKIP grid presented as three blocks behind an approve/edit/reject gate. Presentation leads with a plain-language recommendation rather than scores, and counts come from the validator, never a hand recount. Division of labour: the composer proposes, the human decides, the deterministic validator guards, and the conductor never improvises a grid in prose. A custom grid needs BOTH the scope .md and the scope-grid.json entry, since a .md without a grid entry resolves as all-SKIP. In-flight recompose uses a pending marker written before the gate and deleted the moment it resolves, flips only pending ahead-of-cursor stages, and audits RECOMPOSED instead of hand-editing state.

nodes.label: gate unresolved Sentinel
nodes.rationale: The single non-deterministic gate case, handed back to the conductor because no parser can derive a team's walking-skeleton stance from free-form practices prose. The stage body must not run until the stance is classified and returned to the engine - a deliberate carve-out in an otherwise tool-owned routing surface.

nodes.label: Second-Intent Offer
nodes.rationale: Classifying each new input as continuation, genuinely new work, or plan-reshape is knowledge-work reserved to the conductor because the read-only engine never births alongside a live intent. Default to continuation; on genuine new work offer rather than auto-birth, naming the inferred scope so the human can correct it and leading the affirmative option with 'Yes', since starting a workflow is a mutation gated on a human yes. A reshape request must route through the compose verb, because a freeform mid-flow next would silently advance the current stage instead.

nodes.label: Walking-Skeleton Stance Classification
nodes.rationale: Resolved by reading the '## Walking Skeleton' section across org, team then project memory with the most-specific non-empty statement winning: always/every greenfield feature maps to on, never maps to off, scope-dependent or unspecified defers to the scope's own skeleton declaration.

nodes.label: SENSOR_FAILED Audit Event
nodes.rationale: The common failure surface for every sensor: the event carries an 8-hex fire-id correlator matching the SENSOR_FIRED row in the active record's audit shard, and the structured detail is written under the intent's .aidlc-sensors/<stage-slug>/<sensor>-<fire-id>.md so the finding is inspectable without inflating the audit row.

nodes.label: claim-sources Sensor
nodes.rationale: Deterministic, advisory, document-provenance check over the Intent Capture deliverable SET (not per file), so scaffolding passes until a deliverable exists. It validates citation shape and resolution only, deliberately leaving to the adversarial reviewer the judgement of whether a cited source actually supports the claim. Its Markdown reading is bounded by an asymmetry rule: where full CommonMark is unaffordable, divergence must land as a false failure and never a false pass, so it may demand an unowed citation but must never let unsourced or invisible-tag content through.

nodes.label: linter Sensor
nodes.rationale: Wraps the project's configured linter (eslint default at v0.5.0) on TS/JS outputs, echoing Fowler's Eslint/Semgrep harness-engineering examples. Multi-language auto-detection (ruff, golangci-lint, clippy) is deferred to v0.6.0+ and carried forward as reading the project type from the practices Tech Stack section.

nodes.label: type-check Sensor
nodes.rationale: Wraps the project's configured type-checker (tsc default at v0.5.0) on TS/TSX outputs with a 60s timeout, echoing Fowler's type-checkers example; mypy/go vet/cargo-check detection is deferred to v0.6.0+ via the practices Tech Stack section.

nodes.label: upstream-coverage Sensor
nodes.rationale: Pure derivation from stage frontmatter with no per-stage config: it reads consumes: and checks each upstream artifact is referenced somewhere in the stage's declared deliverables. Coverage is a property of the whole output rather than each file, so a citation in a sibling deliverable counts and scaffolding is excluded from both sides. Accepted reference forms are deliberately broad (standalone slug token, wikilink, backticked filename, producing-stage directory as a path segment) while refusing embedded matches, so 'requirements' inside 'nfr-requirements' does not count.

nodes.label: Inline Source-Tag Register
nodes.rationale: Every substantive paragraph, list item and table row carries a [desc], [scope], [Q<n>], [memory:<id>] or [assumption] tag that must resolve: [desc]/[scope] match aidlc-state.md exactly, memory tags name a visible rule under the cited H2 of the active space's org/team/project files, question tags resolve to filled answers, [scope] only for a workflow-selected signal, [assumption] only inside the assumptions section, and retained assumptions must match an Assumption Confirmation answered exactly 'A. Accept assumptions'. A tag counts only when rendered as literal text, so a link reference definition silently degrades a tag to a link that grounds nothing.

nodes.label: required-sections Sensor
nodes.rationale: Default mode is a deliberately generic content-shape floor (at least two H2 headings) because the framework ships no per-stage heading overrides; teams introduce specific shapes via a template file or the learning loop when there is a real reason.

nodes.label: Template-Override Layer
nodes.rationale: Two override paths with fixed precedence: a resolving memory/templates/<artifact>.md wins over a '## Sensors'-prose override. The file-driven path is preferred because the same template is the skeleton the agent fills, so the produced shape and the checked shape cannot drift; the check passes iff expected headings are a subset of the output and names the missing ones as precise advisory findings. Templates apply only to template-eligible prose artifacts - one resolving for a questions or timestamp marker is ignored with a config warning and the marker keeps the generic floor.

nodes.label: units YAML Edge Block
nodes.rationale: For unit-of-work-dependency.md the sensor additionally requires the fenced yaml units: block to be present, well-formed and cycle-free, reporting ok/absent/malformed/cyclic; anything but ok fails at the gate specifically so a malformed DAG never reaches the runtime compiler that parses it into the batch fan-out.

nodes.label: invoke-swarm Directive
nodes.rationale: Emitted only for an eligible Construction batch under an autonomous grant, and orthogonal to the reserved agent-team stage mode. The live session is the conductor and owns fan-out and retry; aidlc-swarm.ts is a deterministic referee that is consulted, never a loop-owner - prepare forks an isolated worktree per unit so parallel units cannot collide.

nodes.label: Per-Unit Iteration
nodes.rationale: When directive.unit is present the run-stage is one iteration of a for_each unit-of-work Construction stage (the 3.1-3.4 design stages plus code-generation): question flow, summary stop and reviewer all run for THIS unit with --unit threaded through the log commands, artifacts land under construction/<unit>/<stage>/, and the engine - not the conductor - drives the loop.

nodes.label: Reviewer Contract
nodes.rationale: The reviewer receives the stage definition, Q&A file and artifact paths - plus resolved consumes on per-unit stages so cross-unit contract claims can be checked against shared inception artifacts - but deliberately never memory.md or plan.md. Every invocation is bracketed by REVIEW_REQUESTED and REVIEW_COMPLETED receipts, a lost verdict is recovered with --retry-pending against the same unmatched request without consuming an iteration, and in the autonomous swarm a unit is not claimable at finalize merely because check passed.

nodes.label: application-design Stage Runner
nodes.rationale: Generated by aidlc-runner-gen as opt-in packaging over /aidlc --stage application-design --single; the same stage stays reachable via the flag without the skill. Two steps only: ask the engine for the single-stage directive, then report --single --result completed, which records a STAGE_STARTED/STAGE_COMPLETED pair under a synthetic workflow id. The conductor persona is delivered by the engine and must not be loaded by hand.

nodes.label: approval-handoff Stage Runner
nodes.rationale: Generated by aidlc-runner-gen as opt-in packaging over /aidlc --stage approval-handoff --single, identical in shape to every other runner: one directive, one --single report, and an explicit refusal to touch the main workflow's Current Stage.

nodes.label: Conductor Persona Delivery
nodes.rationale: The irreducible execution-quality charter is authored once and baked by the engine into the first run-stage directive's conductor_persona field rather than loaded from a path, so every entry point receives the same charter and no caller can load a stale or partial copy by hand.

nodes.label: run-stage Directive
nodes.rationale: Carries stage_file, consumes, memory_path, rules_in_context, inline_context_paths, mode, gate, unit and single. Context loading is scoped by topology on purpose: lead plus supports on inline, lead only on mob, none on fully dispatched subagent/pipeline - and agent names alone are never loaded context. The branch order is single first, then gate.

nodes.label: Single-Stage Isolation
nodes.rationale: An isolated run keeps the full ritual (summary stop, artifacts, diary, reviewer, verification) but commits under a synthetic workflow id and never advances Current Stage - the tool refuses to. --single is threaded through the checkpoint decision/answer pair and both reviewer log calls precisely so those receipts cannot be mistaken for satisfying the main workflow.

nodes.label: Compiled Stage Graph
nodes.rationale: 32 stages across initialization, ideation, inception, construction and operation, each with phase, ALWAYS/CONDITIONAL execution, lead and support agents and a run mode. The engine reads data/stage-graph.json directly for all routing; the table in the skill is the generated mirror. Only four stages are non-inline: reverse-engineering (pipeline), practices-discovery (subagent), user-stories (mob) and code-generation (subagent).

Overlap is resolved by decomposing each stage's concrete output dimensions and keeping only the UNIQUE ones downstream stages consume.

nodes.label: Minimum viable workflow (expected-value stage selection)
nodes.rationale: The right question is not whether AI can do this in one shot but what the least sufficient safe workflow is for this codebase; each added stage must reduce implementation entropy, failure cost, or verification weakness by more than it costs, and single-shot is valid only when it IS the minimum viable workflow.

nodes.label: Most-Recent Worktree Semantics
nodes.rationale: info walks the audit log end-to-start and returns the latest matching create, matching the user's mental model of 'the live worktree for slug X'; a retry does not create a new event, so output stays stable across retry attempts.

nodes.label: aidlc-worktree info Subcommand
nodes.rationale: A pinned JSON-plus-exit-code contract between the deterministic tool and the LLM's prose composition: the tool resolves slug, path, branch_name, audit_timestamp and merge_held from the audit log so the orchestrator interpolates facts rather than guessing them. Exit 1 mirrors verify's semantics (non-zero is the halt signal), and on a malformed block the tool refuses to guess, leaving flagging and remediation to doctor.

nodes.label: Adaptive Workflow Composer
nodes.rationale: Forced onto a task even when a stock scope would match, so a task that only looks like a stock scope still gets a fitted plan rather than an assumed one.

nodes.label: Approve/Edit/Reject Proposal Gate
nodes.rationale: The composer proposal is held at a human gate before it is authored as a scope and run, so an auto-derived plan never executes unreviewed.

nodes.label: Intent Birth (Initialization as a Phase)
nodes.rationale: Initialization is a phase, not a stage - minting the intent, detecting greenfield/brownfield, and building aidlc-state.md happen together in one deterministic call, which is why no per-init-stage runner exists.

nodes.label: Engine-Delivered Conductor Persona
nodes.rationale: The conductor persona arrives on the first directive conductor_persona field and is adopted for the whole run; skills are explicitly told not to load it by hand so persona selection cannot drift from engine state.

nodes.label: Deterministic Forwarding Loop
nodes.rationale: next, act on directive.kind (run-stage / ask / print / error / done), report, repeat until kind == done. Kept deterministic so the conductor never invents routing; the engine stays the single source of truth for stage order.

nodes.label: Opt-In Packaging (No Second Entry Point)
nodes.rationale: Each runner skill is packaging over a flag on /aidlc, never an alternate entry point: the underlying invocation works without the skill, so the skill set can grow without multiplying engine doors.

nodes.label: State-File Scope Precedence
nodes.rationale: The --scope baked into a scope-runner skill only seeds a fresh workflow; the scope in the state file always wins on an existing workflow, so re-invoking a runner resumes rather than re-scopes.

nodes.label: Single-Stage Isolation
nodes.rationale: A --single run never writes the main workflow Current Stage - the tool refuses to advance it - so a stage can be rehearsed or re-run without disturbing an in-flight workflow.

nodes.label: Kebab-Case Record-Dir Label Derivation
nodes.rationale: A 2-3 word --label becomes the date-prefixed record dir name while the full --arguments text is preserved in audit and state; the description must go through --arguments because intent-create reads it from the flag rather than a positional, and forwarding it bare would silently drop it.

nodes.label: Shift-Left Security
nodes.rationale: Detect in IDE and at commit rather than after deploy; keep early checks fast and non-blocking, then enforcing later - security is shared responsibility, not gatekeeping.

nodes.label: Time-Boxed Security Waivers
nodes.rationale: Exceptions require security team approval and auto-expire so accepted risk cannot become permanent.

nodes.label: Deliberation Rules
nodes.rationale: Independence is preserved until findings are recorded, decisions are never made by vote alone, a supported veto inside a reviewer's exclusive domain blocks PASS, closing or downgrading a finding requires evidence, and the Chair consolidates dissent without erasing it. An unavailable required reviewer makes the review NOT REVIEWABLE rather than substituting a generic majority.

nodes.label: Validation Auditor
nodes.rationale: Sole independent custody reviewer for December 2022: vetoes on any unauthorized access, missing access record, post-result change, overwritten prediction, absent pre-metric hash, or a false second-blind-holdout claim.

nodes.label: Approved Claim Boundary
nodes.rationale: Any geographic, operational, positioning, commercial, multi-year, or arbitrary-location claim exceeding the approved three-station 2022 +1-hour boundary is a blocker.

nodes.label: Comparison-Wide Mask Fairness
nodes.rationale: Pairwise or model-specific masks let models sit different exams, so one comparison-wide mask with equal eligible information and matched windows is required.

nodes.label: IRI-Free ML Boundary
nodes.rationale: No IRI value, residual, target, transformation or derived field may reach ML training or inference, and IRI/GIM modules must not be imported into feature or model code - they are joined only at evaluation time.

nodes.label: Locked-Test Access And Hash-Before-Metrics
nodes.rationale: December 2022 performance may not be accessed before G-05, predictions are written once and never regenerated or overwritten, and the prediction hash precedes any metric.

nodes.label: Model Advancement Test
nodes.rationale: ADVANCE requires all six conditions on frozen evidence, including improvement over persistence on the same mask, co-reported seasonal persistence and climatology, no single-station-driven gain, and interpretation against the target uncertainty budget. A valid DO NOT ADVANCE may still receive a process-gate PASS.

nodes.label: Paired-Loss Estimand And Sign Convention
nodes.rationale: IRI squared loss minus LSTM squared loss with equal-station weighting, so a positive value favours the model; a reversed or unstated sign is a blocker.

nodes.label: Reproducibility And Implementation Checks
nodes.rationale: Python 3.11 exact pins, per-run environment capture, local and Kaggle evidence, a complete CPU path, exactly four governed configs, both fixtures, and critical negative-path tests; the seven-day LSTM fixture is a smoke test, never scientific evidence.

nodes.label: Vector Time-Block Bootstrap
nodes.rationale: 10,000 24-hour vector block replicates carrying all stations together, a 48-hour sensitivity, and a reported cross-station paired-error correlation.

nodes.label: Gate Verdict
nodes.rationale: Exactly one of PASS, CONDITIONAL PASS, FAIL, or NOT REVIEWABLE. CONDITIONAL PASS is barred for an unresolved P0 freeze, missing supervisor approval, unauthorized locked-test access, IRI leakage, protected-hash drift, target-definition ambiguity, or missing primary evidence; NOT REVIEWABLE is returned rather than reviewing around absent authority or evidence.

nodes.label: Independent Evidence Passes
nodes.rationale: Every active reviewer gets the same artifact set and no other reviewer's conclusions before their pass completes, so findings are genuinely independent rather than anchored.

nodes.label: Model Advancement Decision
nodes.rationale: Issued separately from the process verdict because project completion is not model success: a correctly executed negative or inconclusive experiment can pass a process gate while DO NOT ADVANCE blocks promotion of the model or a positive claim.

nodes.label: TEC_Project Governance Overlay Policy
nodes.rationale: AI-DLC approval and TEC governance are separate: AI-DLC may declare a stage complete, but only the human student or supervisor accepts the TEC gate after reading the governance report, and nothing advances while the verdict is FAIL or NOT REVIEWABLE.

nodes.label: Overlay Separation From AI-DLC Conductor
nodes.rationale: The skill is never embedded into AI-DLC's shipped conductor, hooks, stage files, agents, or state machine, so it can be reapplied independently when AI-DLC is upgraded. Vision and Technical Environment stay in the repository rather than being copied into the skill, so the review always reads their current approved versions.

nodes.label: Conflict-Of-Interest Recusal Rule
nodes.rationale: Anyone who built, tuned, selected or materially changed the artifact or model may present evidence but must not chair its final validation decision; if the nominal Chair is conflicted an independent human decision owner is assigned and the AI board stays advisory.

nodes.label: Read-Only Governance Overlay
nodes.rationale: The board reviews and recommends: it does not implement fixes, rewrite approved artifacts, open protected data, approve academic gates, or alter AI-DLC state, and it stops after the recommendation for a human decision.

nodes.label: Graphify Add (URL Ingestion)
nodes.rationale: URL type is auto-detected (YouTube, Twitter/X, arXiv, PDF, image, webpage) and the saved file is merged via the --update pipeline instead of a full rebuild.

nodes.label: Watch Mode With Debounce
nodes.rationale: Code-only changes rebuild via AST with no LLM; doc/paper/image changes only raise a needs_update flag because they require semantic re-extraction. Debounce waits for file activity to stop so a wave of parallel agent writes does not trigger one rebuild per file.

nodes.label: FalkorDB Export
nodes.rationale: Push is preferred over the generated cypher.txt because FalkorDB's GRAPH.QUERY runs one statement at a time and has no bulk script import like Neo4j's cypher-shell.

nodes.label: Graphify MCP Stdio Server
nodes.rationale: Exposes query_graph, get_node, get_neighbors, get_community, god_nodes, graph_stats and shortest_path so other agents can query the graph live; Claude Desktop must be given the absolute interpreter path because it cannot run command substitution.

nodes.label: Agent-Crawlable Wiki Export
nodes.rationale: Runs before cleanup so .graphify_labels.json is still on disk.

nodes.label: Cross-Repo Graph Merge
nodes.rationale: Each repo is built separately then merged with merge-graphs; every node carries a repo attribute so the merged graph can be filtered by origin, and clones are reused on repeat runs.

nodes.label: Native CLAUDE.md Integration
nodes.rationale: Writes a ## graphify section into the project CLAUDE.md so the graph is consulted before codebase questions and rebuilt after code changes without anyone typing /graphify.

nodes.label: Post-Commit Rebuild Hook
nodes.rationale: Triggers once per commit instead of holding a background process, diffs HEAD~1 for changed code files, and re-runs AST extraction only; doc and image changes are left to a manual --update. An existing hook is appended to rather than replaced.

nodes.label: BFS And DFS Traversal Modes
nodes.rationale: BFS answers 'what is X connected to' with nearest-neighbour breadth; DFS traces how X reaches Y along one chain and is depth-limited to 6 so it does not walk the whole graph.

nodes.label: LESSONS.md Reflection
nodes.rationale: reflect --if-stale is deterministic and LLM-free, and no-ops when LESSONS.md is already newer than every input, so a session-start refresh of preferred sources, known dead ends and prior corrections costs almost nothing.

nodes.label: Inline NetworkX Fallback Traversal
nodes.rationale: Used when the graphify query CLI is unavailable, matching nodes the same way the binary does so answers stay consistent.

nodes.label: save-result Work Memory Loop
nodes.rationale: The answer, its cited nodes, and the expanded-token trace are written back so the next --update extracts the Q&A as a graph node, closing a self-improving feedback loop.

nodes.label: Token Budget Ranked Output
nodes.rationale: Nodes are ranked by term overlap and the output is truncated at roughly four characters per token, so the most relevant subgraph survives the cap.

nodes.label: Incremental Update (--update)
nodes.rationale: Only new or changed files are re-extracted, saving tokens and time; files carries the changed subset while all_files carries the full corpus for steps needing corpus-wide context.

nodes.label: AST Structural Extraction
nodes.rationale: Code files are covered structurally by a deterministic AST pass, so semantic subagents are only given content files and never re-read every source file.

nodes.label: Monorepo Subfolder Extraction
nodes.rationale: The skill pipeline always writes to graphify-out/ in the cwd, so running it per subfolder would clobber the same output dir; the CLI is used instead because it places graphify-out/ inside each scanned path before the root-level merge.

nodes.label: Constrained Query Expansion
nodes.rationale: The query CLI matches by case-folded substring plus IDF with no stemming, synonyms, or cross-language matching, so a vocabulary mismatch returns zero hits and the answer collapses to noise. The question is expanded only against tokens actually present in the graph's own label vocabulary - never invented - and the selection is printed so it is auditable; an empty selection stops the query instead of fabricating a search.

nodes.label: Code-Only Change Fast Path
nodes.rationale: When every changed file is code, semantic extraction is skipped entirely because AST is deterministic and no LLM is needed.

nodes.label: Fast Path For Existing Graph
nodes.rationale: When graphify-out/graph.json already exists and the request is a natural-language codebase question, Steps 1-5 are skipped entirely: the graph is already built, so re-detecting and re-extracting would spend tokens to reproduce what is on disk.

nodes.label: Error Handling Standards
nodes.rationale: Fail fast, typed errors, never swallow, propagate with context, separate recoverable from fatal.

nodes.label: File Organization
nodes.rationale: One primary export per file and grouping by feature rather than technical layer.

nodes.label: Function Design Standards
nodes.rationale: Max 30 lines, single responsibility, max 3 parameters, guard clauses, pure where possible.

nodes.label: Code Organization by Feature
nodes.rationale: Co-locates related code, scopes a feature to one directory, and leaves each feature directory a microservice extraction candidate.

nodes.label: Code Organization by Layer
nodes.rationale: Avoided for medium-large projects because it scatters related code across the project.

nodes.label: Dependency Inversion Principle
nodes.rationale: Pass dependencies in rather than constructing them internally.

nodes.label: File Rules
nodes.rationale: Under 300 lines - a longer file usually means the concept does too much.

nodes.label: Function Rules
nodes.rationale: If the function name contains and, split it; boolean switch parameters become two named functions.

nodes.label: Liskov Substitution Principle
nodes.rationale: If an override changes the contract, the inheritance hierarchy itself is wrong.

nodes.label: Result Type Error Handling
nodes.rationale: Preferred over exceptions for expected failures because success and failure become explicit in the type.

nodes.label: Structured JSON Logging
nodes.rationale: Structured fields with correlation IDs enable tracing across services in a way free-text strings cannot.

nodes.label: Try-Catch Hierarchy
nodes.rationale: Catch specific first, let unknowns propagate, catch broadly only at boundaries, never swallow silently.

nodes.label: Touch Target Sizing
nodes.rationale: Minimum 44x44px (Apple HIG) or 48x48px (Material Design).

nodes.label: Feedback and State Patterns
nodes.rationale: Loading, success, error, empty, and confirmation treatments.

nodes.label: Layout Adaptation Patterns
nodes.rationale: Fluid, adaptive, or responsive.

nodes.label: Mobile Performance Considerations
nodes.rationale: Under 3s on 3G, lazy loading, under 200KB initial JS, srcset responsive images.

nodes.label: Navigation Patterns
nodes.rationale: Primary navigation persistent with max 7 items.

nodes.label: Sitemap Structure Patterns
nodes.rationale: Hub-and-spoke, hierarchical, or sequential chosen to match the primary user workflow.

nodes.label: Error Prevention Patterns
nodes.rationale: Undo beats confirmation; disabling invalid options beats post-selection errors.

nodes.label: Progressive Disclosure
nodes.rationale: Every screen needs one clear primary action - overwhelmed users signal too much shown at once.

nodes.label: Mobile-First Breakpoint Strategy
nodes.rationale: Content dictates breakpoints, not device names.

nodes.label: Content Grouping Strategies
nodes.rationale: Group by user task rather than by system structure.

nodes.label: Labeling Taxonomy
nodes.rationale: Labels use the user's language, not internal jargon, and are tested with 5+ representative users.

nodes.label: Navigation Hierarchy Principles
nodes.rationale: Flat beats deep - max 3 nesting levels and every page reachable within 3 clicks.

nodes.label: Nielsen's 10 Usability Heuristics

nodes.label: Metrics Requirements

nodes.label: Scalability Requirement Format

nodes.label: Observability Anti-Patterns

nodes.label: Performance Anti-Requirements

nodes.label: Performance Requirement Definition

nodes.label: Scaling Decision Matrix
