nodes.label: Security Anti-Requirements

nodes.label: RAID log for compliance risks and issues

nodes.rationale: Not all compliance gaps carry equal weight, so remediation is prioritised by data sensitivity and regulatory penalty rather than treated uniformly.

nodes.label: Requirements traceability chain
nodes.rationale: Every downstream artifact must be traceable back to a validated requirement so that no built thing lacks a justification.

nodes.label: Stage observation diary (memory.md)
nodes.rationale: The diary is the only file the conductor maintains by hand; everything else (state fields, checkboxes, audit rows) is tool-owned. Creation is idempotent so a resume never loses accumulated entries, and it is left in place on approval because it is the stage's permanent record and the learnings gate reads it.

nodes.label: Append-only per-clone audit shards
nodes.rationale: State fields, checkboxes, and audit rows are tool-owned silent bookkeeping writes rather than narrated prose, so lifecycle transitions cannot be faked in conversation; the trail is per-clone sharded and append-only, which makes it the canonical source of what happened.

nodes.label: Phase boundary traceability verification
nodes.rationale: Traceability is checked at each phase transition — after the last stage of a phase is approved and before the first stage of the next begins — so missing links and orphaned artifacts surface at the boundary rather than downstream. The Initialization to Ideation transition has no boundary check because there is nothing upstream to trace to.

nodes.label: Question format and tri-mode question flow
nodes.norm_label: question format and tri-mode question flow
nodes.rationale: Guided, self-guided, and chat modes all converge on the same questions file, so the file stays the single source of truth regardless of how the human chose to answer; contradiction detection and overconfidence prevention are mandatory so ambiguity is resolved inside the stage rather than carried forward.

nodes.label: Error severity levels and escalation guidelines
nodes.norm_label: error severity levels and escalation guidelines
nodes.rationale: Critical and High stop and ask immediately with no guessing; Medium attempts resolution then asks; Low is handled silently and logged — so human interruption is rationed to cases where a wrong guess would corrupt the output.

nodes.label: aidlc-orchestrate.ts (next, continue, report, park)
nodes.rationale: The parts that must be exact rather than judged (where the workflow is, the decision log, what runs next) live in deterministic CLI tools instead of LLM prose.

nodes.label: Sensors subsystem (report, never block)
nodes.rationale: Automatic checks run against what gets written but only report; stages pull the sensors they want via a frontmatter import resolved at compile time, so the check set is declared per stage rather than globally enforced.

nodes.label: Stage-runner skills and --single isolated mode
nodes.rationale: A single-stage run is isolated by design and the tool refuses to advance the main workflow, so running one stage for its own sake cannot corrupt the main Current Stage pointer.

nodes.label: The Conductor (execution-quality persona)
nodes.rationale: Splits ownership deliberately: the engine decides which stage runs next and owns all lifecycle bookkeeping, while the conductor owns the irreducible knowledge-work of running that stage well. The persona is baked into the first directive of a session rather than referenced by path, so every entry point receives it identically.

nodes.label: Error recovery and change handling supplement
nodes.norm_label: error recovery and change handling supplement
nodes.rationale: Loaded only on session resume or when a change event is detected mid-stage, as a supplement rather than a replacement, so the main protocol stays the common path and recovery prose does not weigh on every stage.

nodes.label: Stage Protocol (runtime execution behaviour)
nodes.rationale: One protocol referenced by every stage file, covering behaviour (gates, question flow, state tracking) while stage-definition.md covers file format — the two concerns are split so a stage author reads format and a stage runner reads behaviour.

nodes.label: Build and Test stage
nodes.rationale: Runs once after all per-unit stages finish, consuming code-generation outputs across every unit, so build and test instructions are authored against the assembled system rather than per unit in isolation.

nodes.label: Reserved field namespace (when, on_failure, blocks_on, timeout, retry)
nodes.norm_label: reserved field namespace (when, on_failure, blocks_on, timeout, retry)
nodes.rationale: Naming planned primitives before they exist prevents future contributor additions from colliding with them; blocks_on in particular is reserved to split today's overloaded requires_stage, which conflates 'I consume your output' with 'I run after you'.

nodes.label: Learnings ritual (13): tool-as-actor learning loop
nodes.rationale: Detection, surfacing, routing, and writing are deterministic while judgment stays the user's, so learnings cannot be invented by the model. Stage files are immutable framework artefacts and the harness is the mutable surface, with one carve-out for the sensors: import list; a confirmed learning lands in the same method files the resolver already reads, so there is no parallel learnings tier and no widen-to-org path.

nodes.label: Contradictory-inputs recovery (never self-resolve)
nodes.rationale: When inputs from different stages contradict, the contradiction is quoted from both sources and the user decides which takes priority; the agent explicitly must not resolve it by choosing an interpretation, because a silent choice hides a decision the human owns.

nodes.label: New reference material mid-stage is evidence, not a routing instruction
nodes.norm_label: new reference material mid-stage is evidence, not a routing instruction
nodes.rationale: Supplying material is not a request to advance: new material sharpens the current design rather than signalling the design is done, so the workflow stays on the current stage and unit instead of skipping remaining design stages or jumping to code generation.

nodes.label: Recovery source read order (artefacts, diary, audit, state, runtime graph)
nodes.norm_label: recovery source read order (artefacts, diary, audit, state, runtime graph)
nodes.rationale: Outputs first, notes second, timeline third, cursor fourth, summary last — the same way a human picks up someone else's half-finished work. The append-only audit trail is canonical and the other four are reconciled against it on disagreement; the previous session's conversation buffer is unrecoverable by design, so re-orientation comes from these five sources instead of an attempted chat reconstruction.

nodes.label: Execute build and tests with bounded self-fix
nodes.norm_label: execute build and tests with bounded self-fix
nodes.rationale: The stage actually runs the commands it documented and updates the summary with real results rather than instructions alone; on failure it diagnoses and fixes, but the retry budget is capped at two attempts before the failure is logged and escalated to the human at the gate, so it cannot loop indefinitely.

nodes.label: Deliberate exclusion of the linter sensor
nodes.norm_label: deliberate exclusion of the linter sensor
nodes.rationale: linter is intentionally not imported because the canonical lint already runs inside the build pipeline this stage drives; double-firing the framework sensor would produce redundant findings against the same files, and the build's own exit code is the load-bearing signal.

nodes.label: Call Edge Direction And Language Rule
nodes.norm_label: call edge direction and language rule
nodes.rationale: Caller is always the source and callee the target, and calls edges never cross languages because a cross-language call edge is a phantom artifact.

nodes.label: Confidence Score Rubric
nodes.rationale: Five discrete values replace a continuous range because models follow discrete rubrics better: the observed bimodal production distribution (>50% at 0.5, >40% at 0.85+) showed range guidance being collapsed to a binary. Anything that fits none of them is marked AMBIGUOUS instead of scored below 0.4.

nodes.label: Hyperedge
nodes.rationale: Used only when three or more nodes participate in a shared concept or flow that pairwise edges cannot express; capped at three per chunk.

nodes.label: Node ID Format Convention
nodes.rationale: Full repo-relative path with every directory level kept, so same-named files in different directories stay distinct and the LLM id matches the AST extractor's id; filename-only or immediate-parent-only ids create orphan ghost duplicates. No chunk suffix, so the same entity is deterministic across chunks.

nodes.label: Semantically Similar Edge
nodes.rationale: Links concepts that solve the same problem with no structural tie, reserved for genuinely non-obvious cross-cutting similarity so the graph is not flooded with trivial matches.

nodes.label: Verbatim source_file Rule
nodes.rationale: The subagent copies the FILE_LIST path character-for-character because the engine canonicalizes and relativizes downstream; this keeps a full build and an incremental --update on the same base so replace-on-re-extract matches the existing node instead of accumulating duplicates.

nodes.label: Whisper Video And Audio Transcription
nodes.rationale: Video and audio cannot be read directly, so they are transcribed to text first and then treated as doc files by semantic extraction; the transcript JSON is written from Python rather than a shell redirect because Whisper prints progress to stdout and would corrupt the file.

nodes.label: EXTRACTED / INFERRED / AMBIGUOUS Audit Trail
nodes.rationale: Every edge carries its evidential status so a reader can tell an explicit source relationship from a model inference; uncertainty is recorded as AMBIGUOUS rather than dropped or promoted.

nodes.label: Community Detection And Labeling
nodes.rationale: Clustering plus human-readable 2-5 word community names surfaces cross-document connections nobody would think to ask about.

nodes.label: Extraction Cache
nodes.rationale: Cache hits are written and any leftover cache file is deleted when there are none, so the merge step never consumes a stale .graphify_cached.json from a prior run.

nodes.label: Graph Health Check
nodes.rationale: A read-only diagnostic that surfaces edge collapse, dangling/missing endpoints and self-loops - the silent-corruption modes of incremental updates and AST/LLM id mismatches. It never aborts, because the graph is still usable, but the integrity issue must be visible.

nodes.label: Graphify Honesty Rules
nodes.rationale: Never invent an edge, never skip the corpus warning, always show token cost, never hide cohesion behind symbols, never render a >5000-node visualization without warning.

nodes.label: Graphify Python Interpreter Sidecar
nodes.rationale: The resolved uv/pipx/venv interpreter path is saved to graphify-out/.graphify_python so every later step and subcommand runs on the interpreter that actually has graphify importable.

nodes.label: Parallel Semantic Extraction Subagents
nodes.rationale: Doc/paper/image chunks are dispatched to general-purpose subagents in one message because reading files one-by-one is 5-10x slower; Explore is forbidden since it is read-only and would silently drop chunk files.

nodes.label: Whisper Domain Hint Prompt
nodes.rationale: The god-node labels already on disk let the model write the one-sentence domain hint itself, so no separate API call is needed; a video-only corpus falls back to a generic punctuation prompt.

nodes.label: build_merge Replace-On-Re-Extract
nodes.rationale: build_merge reads graph.json directly with no NetworkX round-trip so edge direction survives, and drops every source_file present in the new chunks before merging so stale nodes for changed files cannot survive.

nodes.label: Cluster-Only Rerun
nodes.rationale: graphify cluster-only is self-contained and Steps 5-9 must not be re-run after it, because they read intermediate files that the prior build's cleanup already deleted and would raise FileNotFoundError.

nodes.label: prune_sources Deletion Pruning
nodes.rationale: prune_sources is restricted to genuinely deleted files: with root= passed it relativizes to the same base as the freshly merged nodes, so adding changed files there would delete the content just re-extracted. root= is required or nothing is pruned and stale nodes accumulate every update.

nodes.label: ADR Lifecycle States
nodes.rationale: Proposed, Accepted, Deprecated, Superseded. Superseding is bidirectional - the new ADR links back and the old one forward - so a reader landing on a stale decision is never left following it.

nodes.label: Alternatives Considered Section
nodes.rationale: Omitting alternatives makes the decision look unconsidered, and omitting negative consequences creates false confidence. Being honest about trade-offs builds trust, so Positive/Negative/Neutral consequences are all mandatory.

nodes.label: ADR Numbering Convention
nodes.rationale: Zero-padded sequential numbers never reused even when deprecated, kebab-case suffix, one index.md listing status and a one-line summary, so a number always resolves to exactly one decision for the life of the project.

nodes.label: ADR Creation Threshold
nodes.rationale: Create one when the decision is hard to reverse, spans teams, has cost/performance/security weight, or was debated - disagreement itself means the reasoning needs recording. Skip routine or trivially reversible choices, because granular ADRs dilute the journal.

nodes.label: Architectural Style Selection Matrix
nodes.rationale: Each style is paired with an explicit Avoid When column - modular monolith fails when independent per-module scaling is needed, microservices when the team is small, event-driven when strong consistency is required everywhere - so selection is driven by system characteristics rather than fashion.

nodes.label: Component Boundary Identification
nodes.rationale: A boundary is correct when the component has one nameable responsibility, owns its data, absorbs internal change without ripple, tests in isolation, and exposes a clear public API. Red flags: components that always deploy together, circular dependencies, pass-through proxies, and shared tables written by multiple components.

nodes.label: Reverse Engineering Synthesis Checklist
nodes.rationale: Eight ordered steps applied to Developer code-scan results: identify the dominant style or its absence, map components to bounded contexts, trace data flow, flag coupling hotspots by fan-in/fan-out, find missing boundaries (god classes, shared state), check test coverage against architectural risk, contrast observed with intended patterns, and emit a component inventory rated healthy/at-risk/degraded.

nodes.label: Microservices
nodes.rationale: Justified by independent deployment, divergent scaling needs, polyglot requirements, and mature DevOps/observability - not by size alone. Each service owns its database, communicates only via APIs or events, and assumes every remote call can fail; the cost is distributed-system complexity, per-service operational overhead, and hard integration testing.

nodes.label: Bounded Contexts
nodes.rationale: The same real-world concept means different things per context - Customer is leads and revenue in Sales, tickets and SLAs in Support, invoices and credit limit in Billing - so each context owns its data and logic with no shared database, and may pick its own stack and deployment strategy. Heuristic: if two concepts change for different reasons they belong in different contexts.

nodes.label: Review Comment Format
nodes.rationale: A single Review section appended to the primary artifact, carrying verdict, reviewer, ISO date obtained from a real shell date command rather than guessed, iteration number, a findings table with severity/location/recommendation, validation tool results with interpretation, and a summary. On later iterations the section is replaced, never duplicated.

nodes.label: Finding Severity Levels
nodes.rationale: Critical means failure at implementation or runtime and always blocks; Major means significant rework and blocks past two; Minor never blocks.

nodes.label: Validation Tool Execution
nodes.rationale: Tools listed by the stage definition are run via shell before the review is written, and their output is interpreted rather than pasted - a tool failure can be acceptable with documented rationale.

nodes.label: Rationale Quality Standard
nodes.rationale: The gate is only as good as the rationale, so each SKIP gets one vetoable line naming the stage, what it would have produced, and why this task does not need that artifact; each EXECUTE names the component it reduces and that no other EXECUTE stage delivers that reduction. Not needed is not a rationale.

nodes.label: Architecture Decision Records
nodes.rationale: ADRs create a decision journal that explains WHY the architecture looks the way it does. Written for a future reader with no context, because the code shows what was built and only the ADR explains why.

nodes.label: ADR as Decision Tool, Not Documentation
nodes.norm_label: adr as decision tool, not documentation
nodes.rationale: Create the ADR BEFORE implementation: it is a decision tool, not documentation. Writing ADRs after the fact is listed as the first common mistake, because a retrospective ADR cannot influence the decision it describes.

nodes.label: Cross-Unit Contract Verification Bound
nodes.rationale: Scope is the passed artifacts plus the shared inception contracts (components.md, component-methods.md, services.md, unit-of-work.md) - not sibling units' functional-design prose, and never via grep, glob, or shell patterns spanning sibling unit paths. A named integration point is spot-checked by opening the owning file resolved through the shared contracts, never by sweeping the sibling unit.

nodes.label: Reviewer Stance
nodes.rationale: The reviewer did not produce the work and deliberately has no access to the builder's plan.md or memory.md, so the design is judged on whether a developer could implement it without guessing. READY means implementable, not perfect.

nodes.label: Broken Access Control
nodes.rationale: Deny by default and verify object-level access to prevent IDOR.

nodes.label: Cryptographic Failures
nodes.rationale: TLS 1.2+ in transit, AES-256 at rest, bcrypt/argon2 for passwords, never roll custom crypto.

nodes.label: Data Classification Tiers and Controls
nodes.rationale: Public, internal, confidential, restricted with per-tier at-rest, in-transit, access and retention controls.

nodes.label: Injection
nodes.rationale: Parameterized queries, contextual output encoding, CSP headers.

nodes.label: Trust Boundary
nodes.rationale: Once data passes the boundary and becomes a domain type, internal code must not re-validate - trusting the boundary keeps domain logic focused on business rules.

nodes.label: Authentication Patterns
nodes.rationale: Session-based for server-rendered apps, JWT for SPAs and APIs with access token in memory and refresh token in HttpOnly cookie, OAuth2 authorization code with PKCE and never implicit flow.

nodes.label: Authorization Patterns
nodes.rationale: RBAC for well-defined hierarchies, ABAC for context-dependent policy, and object-level checks because client-provided ownership claims are never trusted.

nodes.label: Insecure Design
nodes.rationale: Threat model during design, not after, and separate business logic from security controls.

nodes.label: Conversation Language Preserved Tokens
nodes.rationale: Literals a stage spells in backticks stay English character-for-character because engines compare filled answers against the literal; only the prose around them is localized.

nodes.label: Conversation Language Resolution
nodes.rationale: A delegated agent never sees the conversation, so the orchestrator restates the language in every brief; the brief is authoritative because it is regenerated per dispatch and can never be staler than a persisted rule, and project.md outranks team.md because only project.md ever records a switch.

nodes.label: Conversation Language Stability
nodes.rationale: Only an explicit human request switches the language, and it takes effect immediately; persistence via the human-gated learnings ritual is a separate step, and direct memory edits are forbidden because they skip the audit event, duplicate key, and admission conflict-check. A new session re-resolves rather than defaulting to English.

nodes.label: Trunk-Based Development Default
nodes.rationale: All work merges to main via short-lived branches because long-lived branches accumulate merge debt; multiple environments are gated by tags or deployment configs rather than long-lived release branches.

nodes.label: Walking Skeleton Ceremony Toggle

nodes.label: AI-DLC (AI-Driven Development Life Cycle)
nodes.rationale: Work advances idea-to-code in ordered steps that each stop at a human approval gate, so nothing advances without the user's say-so and the plan, depth, and direction stay changeable at any gate.

nodes.label: Architect Agent
nodes.rationale: Thinks in patterns and trade-offs rather than specific services; boundaries are treated as the architecture because getting component boundaries right matters more than internal implementation detail, and reversible decisions are preferred over perfect ones.

nodes.label: AWS Platform Agent
nodes.rationale: Infrastructure is code, not configuration: console changes count as drift and must be reconciled or reverted, and any environment creatable by code must also be destroyable by code because orphaned resources are hidden cost leaks.

nodes.label: Compliance Agent
nodes.rationale: Support-only by design: regulatory requirements are identified in Ideation and tracked through Operation because discovering compliance gaps at release is a project failure; the agent educates and the team executes.

nodes.label: Design Agent
nodes.rationale: Designs for scannability and predictability to lower cognitive load, favours error prevention over error messages, and treats WCAG accessibility as a baseline rather than a stretch goal; for non-UI initiatives it produces system context diagrams and API experience designs instead.

nodes.label: Developer Agent
nodes.rationale: Working code over perfect code (refactor in later iterations, not during generation), convention over configuration so consistency with the existing codebase beats personal preference, and scan-before-build because the thoroughness of the reverse-engineering code scan determines the quality of the architect's synthesis.

nodes.label: DevSecOps Agent
nodes.rationale: Security is embedded in every phase rather than bolted on at the end: the agent takes compliance requirements identified in Ideation and turns them into controls, threat models, scanning pipelines, and runtime monitoring, designing as if the perimeter is already breached.

nodes.label: Operations Agent
nodes.rationale: Collects comprehensive telemetry but pages humans only for user-impacting issues, because alert fatigue degrades incident response faster than missing alerts; it is the bridge that returns production insight to Ideation, since insight that does not flow back is wasted learning.

nodes.label: Pipeline & Deploy Agent
nodes.rationale: Treats every commit as a release candidate and keeps pipelines to minutes because slow pipelines encourage batching and batching increases risk; bypassing a quality gate is classified as an incident rather than a shortcut, and a deployment is not done until smoke tests confirm health.

nodes.label: Product Agent
nodes.rationale: No requirement without a source, because invented requirements waste effort; a requirement that cannot be verified by a concrete test is a wish, not a requirement; and stories are cut as vertical slices rather than horizontal layers.

nodes.label: Quality Agent
nodes.rationale: Tests validate the specified behaviour rather than the chosen implementation; the suite is shaped as a pyramid not an ice cream cone; and coverage is treated as a guide because 100% line coverage with meaningless assertions is worse than 70% with thoughtful tests.

nodes.label: Environment parity (differ only in scale, never topology)
nodes.norm_label: environment parity (differ only in scale, never topology)
nodes.rationale: Dev, staging, and production must differ only in scale so that environment-specific behaviour is classified as a deployment bug rather than an accepted difference.

nodes.label: Data classification drives control selection
nodes.rationale: Classify first, control second: without classification every control is either insufficient or wasteful, and a control without proof of operation is a control that does not exist.

nodes.label: PRACTICES_OVERRIDE judgement
nodes.rationale: When a bolt-plan marker and team practices disagree, practices wins and the divergence is recorded as an explicit override event, because practices are the team's standing voice while a bolt-plan marker is one workflow's interpretation.

nodes.label: Walking-skeleton stance classification (gate: unresolved)
nodes.rationale: Most gate values are deterministic, but the first Construction Bolt depends on a stance no parser can derive from free-form practices prose, so the engine defers it as gate: unresolved, receives the classification back via report --skeleton-stance, and still owns the transition. Judgment is delegated; control is not.

nodes.label: Strict-additive five-layer rule chain (org to team to project to phase to stage)
nodes.norm_label: strict-additive five-layer rule chain (org to team to project to phase to stage)
nodes.rationale: Method files are authored once at the workspace root and imported by reference, never copied, so every harness reads one hand-editable source of truth; narrower layers may only add specialisation, and a contradiction with broader policy is rejected at the learning admission check before it reaches disk.

nodes.label: Cache Placement Decision Matrix
nodes.rationale: Placement, TTL and invalidation are chosen together per scenario (CDN edge with version-hash URLs, gateway with event-driven purge, application cache write-through/behind, session store with explicit delete). Never cache data that must be strongly consistent, always set a TTL because unbounded caches become stale data stores, and target above 90% hit ratio on read-heavy paths.

nodes.label: Circuit Breaker State Machine
nodes.rationale: Closed counts failures and opens at threshold; Open fails fast without calling downstream; Half-Open probes with a single request and closes on success or re-opens on failure - failing fast is the point, since queuing calls to a dead dependency is what propagates the outage.

nodes.label: Failure Mode Checklist
nodes.rationale: Per component: what happens on unavailability, doubled response time, over-capacity throughput, and corrupted dependency data; is there a graceful degradation path; what is the blast radius (user, tenant, region, global); and what is the recovery procedure. Blast radius and recovery are asked explicitly so they are designed rather than discovered.

nodes.label: Resilience Pattern Selection Table
nodes.rationale: Six patterns chosen by failure-mode analysis with concrete starting configuration: circuit breaker (threshold 5, timeout 30s), bulkhead per dependency, retry with exponential backoff plus jitter, timeout on every external call without exception, fallback when degraded mode beats total failure, rate limiter to shield downstream from upstream bursts.

nodes.label: SLI/SLO and Error Budget Definition
nodes.rationale: SLIs are ratios (successful/total, below-threshold/total, correct/total), SLOs state a target over a window, and the error budget is 1 minus the SLO - 99.9% is 43.2 minutes of downtime per 30 days, which converts an abstract target into a spendable allowance.

nodes.label: Bulkhead Isolation
nodes.rationale: Per-dependency thread pools, connection pools, or process separation stop one failing component from consuming all system resources. Sizing is a trade-off: too small causes needless rejection, too large defeats the isolation.

nodes.label: Cache-Aside (Lazy Loading)
nodes.rationale: The default pattern, with the application managing the cache explicitly. Its named risk is a thundering herd on cold start or cache failure, mitigated by cache warming at startup and request coalescing.

nodes.label: Cache Invalidation Rules
nodes.rationale: TTL on every item because stale data is worse than a cache miss; explicit invalidation on write where consistency matters; never cache error responses; a hit ratio below 80% means the cache is not helping.

nodes.label: Circuit Breaker Pattern
nodes.rationale: Prevents cascading failure when a downstream service is unavailable. Breakers are per-dependency rather than global, state transitions are logged for observability, and a meaningful fallback (cached data, degraded response, queued retry) is required for the open state to be useful.

nodes.label: Connection Pooling
nodes.rationale: Reuses expensive connections instead of creating one per request, with min/max size, acquisition timeout, idle timeout, and a max lifetime that recycles connections by age to prevent stale ones. Sizing formula: RPS x average duration in seconds x 1.5 buffer.

nodes.label: Graceful Degradation
nodes.rationale: Reduce functionality instead of failing entirely, via feature flags, stale cached fallback with an outdated indicator, defaults, queue-for-later writes, or read-only mode. Every dependency is mapped to a priority tier (critical path, important, nice to have) with its degradation strategy defined before production launch.

nodes.label: Load Balancing Algorithms and Health Checks
nodes.norm_label: load balancing algorithms and health checks
nodes.rationale: Round robin for homogeneous instances, least connections for variable request duration, weighted for mixed capacity, consistent hashing to preserve cache affinity. Shallow checks drive load-balancer routing while deep dependency checks drive alerting, so a downstream outage does not eject every healthy instance from the pool.

nodes.label: Rate Limiting
nodes.rationale: Token bucket allows controlled bursts, sliding window smooths boundary bursts, fixed window is simplest but permits 2x at the boundary. Applied at the gateway for external consumers and per-user or per-tenant for fairness, returning 429 with Retry-After and communicating remaining quota in response headers.

nodes.label: Retry with Exponential Backoff
nodes.rationale: Always add jitter, because without it retries from multiple clients synchronize into a thundering herd. Cap retries at 3-5 to avoid resource exhaustion, retry only transient failures (429, 5xx, timeouts, resets) and never 400 or 403, and ensure idempotency via idempotency keys.

nodes.label: Write-Behind (Write-Back) Cache
nodes.rationale: Lowest write latency because only the cache write is synchronous, accepting data loss if the cache fails before the batched async write lands - suitable only where brief inconsistency is tolerable.

nodes.label: Write-Through Cache
nodes.rationale: Cache stays consistent with the database at the cost of two synchronous writes per mutation, so it fits only where reads vastly outnumber writes.

nodes.label: Pillar: Reliability
nodes.rationale: Multi-AZ for critical components, auto scaling in both directions, fault isolation via bulkheads, circuit breakers and timeouts on all remote calls, and chaos engineering. Untested backup restores are called out explicitly: backups that exist but have never been restored are not a recovery capability.

nodes.label: Non-Functional Requirement Design Patterns
nodes.rationale: Addresses the gap between it works and it works reliably at scale.

nodes.label: Color Contrast Requirements
nodes.rationale: 4.5:1 normal text, 3:1 large text and UI components; color alone must never carry meaning.

nodes.label: Keyboard Navigation Requirements
nodes.rationale: Visible focus indicator, logical tab order, no keyboard traps, skip-to-content first.

nodes.label: Text Alternatives and Alt Text
nodes.rationale: Decorative images use empty alt so screen readers skip them.

nodes.label: WCAG 2.1 Level AA
nodes.rationale: The standard target for most applications and legally required in many jurisdictions.

nodes.label: First Rule of ARIA
nodes.rationale: Native HTML is always preferable - a button element beats a div with role=button; use ARIA only when HTML cannot express the semantics.

nodes.label: POUR Principles
nodes.rationale: Perceivable, Operable, Understandable, Robust - the four organising principles of WCAG.

nodes.label: Accessibility Testing Approach
nodes.rationale: Automated scanning catches only about 30% of issues, so keyboard, screen reader, zoom, and color-blindness passes are required.

nodes.label: Modal and Dialog Patterns
nodes.rationale: Modals suit confirmation and small focused input; nested modals and large content are always wrong.

nodes.label: data-testid Attributes
nodes.rationale: Stable semantic kebab-case ids on every interactive element so E2E, integration and accessibility automation does not break on code changes or generated ids.

nodes.label: Conventional Commits Subject Contract
nodes.rationale: `<type>(<scope>): <imperative summary>`, imperative mood, <=50 chars preferred with a hard cap of 72, no trailing period, body wrapped at 72 and issue refs at the end.

nodes.label: No AI Attribution in Commit Messages
nodes.norm_label: no ai attribution in commit messages
nodes.rationale: No 'this commit does X', no first person, no 'as requested by' (use a Co-authored-by trailer), and no AI-attribution line unless the user's own rule requires an Assisted-by trailer — in which case it goes in as a trailer, not prose.

nodes.label: 65% Output-Token Reduction Benchmark
nodes.rationale: Measured, not estimated: 65% of output tokens cut with full accuracy preserved, which is the justification the mode rests on.

nodes.label: One-Line Review Comment Format
nodes.rationale: `L<line>: <severity> <problem>. <fix>.` — one line per finding, dropping 'I noticed that', hedging, and restatement of what the diff already shows, while keeping exact line numbers, backticked symbols and a concrete fix.

nodes.label: Severity Emoji Taxonomy
nodes.rationale: Red bug, yellow risk, blue nit, question mark query — a single glyph carries the severity that would otherwise cost a sentence.

nodes.label: Six Caveman Intensity Levels
nodes.rationale: lite / full (default) / ultra / wenyan-lite / wenyan-full / wenyan-ultra, so compression can be dialled to context rather than being all-or-nothing.

nodes.label: User Language Preservation Rule
nodes.rationale: Compress the style, not the language: reply in the user's dominant language regardless of example text. 'Drop articles' applies to article languages only — where small markers carry case or role (particles, postpositions) they are grammar, not filler, so politeness and filler are compressed instead.

nodes.label: Wenyan Classical Chinese Modes
nodes.rationale: 80-90% character reduction (characters, not tokens) via classical sentence patterns and particles; classical characters are permitted only in wenyan modes, never swapped in at other levels to shrink output.

nodes.label: Caveman Commit Overview
nodes.rationale: Terse Conventional Commits, why over what. Outputs only the message: it does not stage, commit, or amend.

nodes.label: Caveman Commit Message Generator
nodes.rationale: Why over what — the diff already says what changed, so the message spends its budget on the non-obvious reason.

nodes.label: Caveman Mode Overview
nodes.rationale: Talk like smart caveman: same brain, fewer tokens. Compresses every model response, dropping articles, filler, pleasantries and hedging while keeping technical detail, code blocks, error strings and symbols exact.

nodes.label: Caveman Review Overview
nodes.rationale: One-line PR comments, no throat-clearing. Output only: it does not approve, request changes, or run linters.

nodes.label: Caveman Communication Mode
nodes.rationale: Respond terse like smart caveman: all technical substance stays, only fluff dies. Pattern is `[thing] [action] [reason]. [next step].`

nodes.label: Mandatory Commit Body Cases
nodes.rationale: Always include a body for breaking changes, security fixes, data migrations, and reverts — never compress these into a subject alone, because future debuggers need the context that the diff cannot supply.

nodes.label: Review Auto-Clarity Exemptions
nodes.rationale: Terse mode is dropped for CVE-class security findings, architectural disagreements, and onboarding contexts where the author needs the why; terse resumes for the rest.

nodes.label: Auto-Clarity Override
nodes.rationale: Drop caveman for security warnings, irreversible-action confirmations, multi-step sequences where fragment order risks misread, cases where compression itself creates technical ambiguity, and when the user re-asks — then resume. Token savings never outrank comprehension where a misread is costly.

nodes.label: Persisted-Output Boundary
nodes.rationale: Anything persisted outside the chat — code, comments, commits, docs, issue/PR text, memory files, third-party messages — is written in normal prose, because compression that reads fine in-session becomes an unexplained artefact once it outlives the conversation. /caveman-compress is the one exemption.

nodes.label: No Invented Abbreviations or Causal Arrows
nodes.norm_label: no invented abbreviations or causal arrows
nodes.rationale: Invented abbreviations (cfg/impl/req/res/fn) tokenize the same as the full word, so they save zero tokens while costing the reader decode effort; the full word is cheaper AND clearer. Causal arrows are their own token and likewise save nothing. Standard well-known acronyms (DB/API/HTTP) remain fine.

nodes.label: Mode Persistence Rule
nodes.rationale: Active every response with no revert after many turns and no filler drift; still active if unsure; off only on explicit 'stop caveman' / 'normal mode'. Also forbids self-reference — never announce or name the style.

nodes.label: Design Pattern Checklist
nodes.rationale: Four gates per pattern decision: problem fit (a specific problem, not a hypothetical one), complexity cost, team familiarity without the architect present, and testing impact. Repository, CQRS, Saga, Strategy, and Adapter each carry a stated when-to-use.

nodes.label: CQRS (Command Query Responsibility Segregation)
nodes.rationale: Apply only when read and write models genuinely diverge. Read models are disposable and rebuildable from the event stream, which is what makes tailoring them to UI needs safe; the cost is two models, synchronization, and eventual consistency - overkill for simple CRUD.

nodes.label: Pattern Decision Framework
nodes.rationale: Start with a modular monolith unless there are proven reasons not to; extract to microservices only when team autonomy or independent scaling demands it; use serverless for event-driven glue rather than core request-response APIs; apply CQRS only on genuine read/write divergence; use hexagonal in the domain layer always.

nodes.label: Event-Driven Architecture
nodes.rationale: Producers do not know their consumers, which buys loose coupling, independent scaling, and a natural audit trail at the price of eventual consistency, ordering and deduplication complexity, and debugging that requires distributed tracing. Three sub-patterns: event notification, event-carried state transfer, event sourcing.

nodes.label: Hexagonal Architecture (Ports and Adapters)
nodes.rationale: The domain depends on nothing external; ports are defined by the domain and adapters translate. Recommended in the domain layer regardless of the outer architectural style, because it is what lets tests run against in-memory adapters with no database or network.

nodes.label: Architecture Migration Paths
nodes.rationale: Modular monolith to microservices extracts one module at a time via strangler fig, starting with the least coupled. The reverse path is legitimate: consolidate when services are too small, team boundaries shift, or operational cost exceeds benefit.

nodes.label: Modular Monolith
nodes.rationale: The default choice for a new product: one deployable with explicit interfaces between data-owning modules and acyclic declared dependencies. Accepts all-or-nothing scaling and shared technology in exchange for simple deployment, debugging, and cross-module refactoring; extract to services later when boundaries are proven.

nodes.label: Aggregates and Aggregate Roots
nodes.rationale: Exactly one root per aggregate is the only externally referenceable entity, so all changes route through it and invariants hold. Transactions must not span aggregates and other aggregates are referenced by ID; large aggregates cause contention, so needing a cross-aggregate transaction is a signal the boundaries are wrong.

nodes.label: Anti-Corruption Layer
nodes.rationale: Isolates a clean domain model from a legacy or external model by translating between them, so when the external system changes only the ACL needs updating.

nodes.label: Context Mapping Patterns
nodes.rationale: Seven named inter-context relationships (Shared Kernel, Customer-Supplier, Conformist, Anti-Corruption Layer, Open Host Service, Published Language, Separate Ways), each selected by team relationship rather than technology - Conformist when upstream has no incentive to accommodate you, Separate Ways when integration costs more than it returns.

nodes.label: Domain Events
nodes.rationale: Past-tense facts named EntityPastTenseVerb, carrying event ID, timestamp, aggregate ID and payload-at-the-time. They are the primary integration mechanism between bounded contexts, which is what makes publishers independent of subscribers.

nodes.label: Entities
nodes.rationale: Defined by identity that persists across state changes, not by attributes: two customers with the same name are different customers if their IDs differ.

nodes.label: Event Storming
nodes.rationale: A seven-step colour-coded workshop (events, commands, actors, aggregates, context boundaries, policies) that surfaces natural bounded-context boundaries, integration points, and complexity hot spots from the domain experts rather than from the code.

nodes.label: Repository Pattern
nodes.rationale: One repository per aggregate root, interface in the domain layer and implementation in infrastructure, returning fully constituted aggregates. Complex query logic belongs in separate read models rather than in repositories.

nodes.label: Value Objects
nodes.rationale: Immutable and identity-free - equality is over all attributes, so two Money objects with the same amount and currency are interchangeable. Preferred over primitives because an email is not just a string.

nodes.label: Horizontal Scaling Strategies
nodes.rationale: Stateless services, sharding, read replicas (above 10:1 read:write, accepting replication lag), event-driven decoupling, and CQRS. Shard keys need high cardinality, even distribution, query locality and immutability, because changing a shard key forces a data migration.

nodes.label: Architecture Patterns
nodes.rationale: No pattern is universally best - each encodes trade-offs between complexity, scalability, team autonomy, and operational cost.

nodes.label: Domain-Driven Design Patterns
nodes.rationale: DDD aligns software design with business reality so the code structure mirrors how the business thinks and operates.
